[Triton/Gluon] [gfx950] [dsv4.1-flash] mHC fused kernel
body:
Currently in dsv4.1-flash for gfx950,
Prefill (num_tokens >= 1024) uses 5 different kernels for mHC:
- `mhc_post_kernel`
- `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum`
- `mhc_pre_big_fuse`
- `_mhc_pre_mix_kernel`
- `_hc_head_reduce_store_kernel`

and decode (num_tokens < 1024) uses 4 kernels for mHC: 
- `mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum`
- `mhc_pre_big_fuse`
- `_mhc_pre_mix_kernel`
- `_hc_head_reduce_store_kernel`
 
and then a kernel for rmsnorm on the input to the attention/moe block `add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel`

We fuse these kernels and replace them with a main kernel (`_mhc_post_pre_delayed_main_kernel`) and reduce kernel (`_mhc_post_pre_delayed_reduce_kernel`).

On a per seam basis (mHC work between two sub-layers) the fused kernel has a speedup of 1.16x for prefill and a speedup of 1.47x for decode compared to the unfused kernels (measured from an e2e trace of `ISL 1024` / `OSL 32` / `CONC 32` / `num_prompts 32` / `max-num-batched-tokens 16384`):

---------------------------------------------------------

| Prefill unfused (T=16316) | Time per seam us |
|--------|--------|
| mhc_post_kernel | 242.1 |
| mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum | 205.9|
| mhc_pre_big_fuse | 125.8 |
| _mhc_pre_mix_kernel | 5.8 |
| _hc_head_reduce_store_kernel | 155.7 | 
| add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel | 53.9 |
| **Unfused total** | **789.2** |

| Prefill fused (T=16316) | Time per seam us |
|--------|--------|
| main kernel | 626.4 |
| reduce kernel | 56.5 |
| **Fused total** | **682.9** |
| **Speedup** | **1.16x** |

--------------------------------------------------------------

| Decode unfused (T=192) | Time per seam us |
|--------|--------|
| mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum | 11.5 |
| mhc_pre_big_fuse | 5.8 |
| _mhc_pre_mix_kernel | 4.2 |
| _hc_head_reduce_store_kernel | 4.5 | 
| add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel | 3.9 |
| **Unfused total** | **29.9** |

| Decode fused (T=192) | Time per seam us |
|--------|--------|
| main kernel | 12.1 |
| reduce kernel | 8.3 |
| **Fused total** | **20.4** |
| **Speedup** | **1.47x** |

title: fix: custom_all_reduce ci hang
body:
## Motivation

test_custom_allreduce.py hangs in CI, killed at the 1h timeout (3600.452s). The hang is inside the test (earlier shards pass; the TCPStore/CudaIPC lines are benign teardown noise). It stalls mid group/CA init on a late shape and ends with `resource_tracker: leaked 6 semaphore / 1 shared_memory objects`.

## Technical Details

root case
Per-shape teardown is entirely GC/`__del__`-dependent; nothing is released deterministically at the destroy() sites:
    - CudaCommunicator.destroy() only drops ca_comm/qr_comm refs.
    - CustomAllreduce.close() never freed self._pool (meta + up to 1GB input).
    - GroupCoordinator.destroy() drops mq_broadcaster; its psm_* shm segment (1<<22 = 4MB, matching the log's buffer_handle) is only unlinked in ShmRingBuffer.__del__.
  The psm segment + semaphores outlive the process, so a killed rank / no-GC exit leaks them into /dev/shm. Across the spawn-per-shape sweep this accumulates; on a small /dev/shm (Docker default 64MB) a later 4MB MessageQueue create blocks inside collective init and peers deadlock. Explains "passes locally, hangs in CI".

fix
(teardown only, no allreduce path touched; all close() idempotent)
  - shm_broadcast.py: ShmRingBuffer.close() and MessageQueue.close()/__del__ (unlink psm + zmq context.destroy); store the zmq Context on self.
  - parallel_state.py: GroupCoordinator.destroy() calls mq_broadcaster.close().
  - communicator_cuda.py: `_owns_comms = reuse_from is None`; destroy() closes ca/qr only when owner (borrowed comms not disposed twice).
  - custom_all_reduce.py: IPCBuffer.close()/IPCBufferPool.close(); CustomAllreduce.close() releases self._pool after dispose (gfx1250 proxy hasattr-guarded).
## Test Plan

watch -n1 'ls /dev/shm/psm_* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; df -h /dev/shm | tail -1'
python op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_custom_allreduce.py -t 8
before: psm_* grows until /dev/shm full → hang; after: returns to baseline, sweep completes

## Test Result

need see ci

title: [Triton/Gluon] [fix] moe_gemm_mxfp8: zero-init output, graph-safe routing, skip redundant copy
body:
## Motivation

Three defects in the `moe_gemm_mxfp8` wrapper. They are grouped because they share one file pair and one theme: how the wrapper handles its output buffer, its routing conversion, and its weight layout.

### 1. Uninitialized output buffer

The kernel writes only rows covered by `ExptHist`/`ExptOffs`, that is `[0, sum(group_sizes))`. A caller that deliberately excludes rows, such as a foreign expert under EP or `-1` top-k padding, leaves the tail of `torch.empty` holding whatever the caching allocator last put there.

Those rows are not safe to ignore. A NaN there survives a downstream `* 0` mask, because `NaN * 0 == NaN`, and the top-k reduction spreads it across the whole token. The failure depends on allocator state, so it passes smoke tests and corrupts output later.

The reference in `op_tests/triton_tests/moe/test_moe_gemm_mxfp8.py` already builds its expected result with `torch.zeros`, so this change makes the kernel match its own test.

### 2. `group_sizes_to_expt_tensors` blocks CUDA graph capture

```python
total_blocks = int(n_blocks_per_expert.sum().item())  # single sync at end
```

`.item()` is a device to host sync, so the call fails under graph capture with `hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`. vLLM captures the MoE forward, so the op cannot be used there today.

This is also unfinished review feedback on #5658. Comment [r4045560427](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5658#discussion_r4045560427) asked for the mapping to be built "with tensor operations (or reuse the existing GPU-side helper)". The per-expert Python loop was removed; the final `.sum().item()` stayed.

The fix reuses the pattern that `build_block_mapping()` in this same file already documents. Every expert wastes at most one partial block, so `cdiv(total_tokens, block_m) + E` bounds the real count with no sync. Surplus slots are stamped `ExptData = -1`, which the kernel already returns early on (`moe_op_gemm_a8w8.py:271-273`). Verified over 2000 random routings.

`total_tokens` is optional and defaults to `None`, which preserves the exact legacy path for existing callers.

### 3. The weight is re-copied on every call

```python
rhs_kn = rhs.permute(0, 2, 1).contiguous()
w_scale_kn = w_scale.permute(0, 2, 1).contiguous()
```

MoE expert weights are static after load, so this re-materializes the whole tensor on every invocation. That costs 2.4 ms for `rhs` alone at `E=32, N=2048, K=6144` on gfx942, and it transiently doubles the weight footprint. Callers that already store K-major now get a view instead.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest op_tests/triton_tests/moe/test_moe_gemm_mxfp8.py -v
```

## Test Result

MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3. Existing tests pass unchanged.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| correctness, 13 shape/layout configs | cosine >= 0.999999 vs fp32 |
| NK vs KN inputs | bitwise identical output |
| CUDA graph capture + replay | fails on main, passes here |
| NaN-poisoned allocator, half-foreign map | 100% NaN before, 0/16384 after |

Shapes cover `K=96` and `K=32`, which exercise the partial and single K-block cases, plus ragged group sizes `[0,7,64,1,100,0,84,0]` including zero-token experts.




## Notes for reviewers

Please add `ci:triton-300x`. The default Triton CI targets gfx950, and these paths are exercised on gfx942.

A companion kernel-side perf change lives on `akii96:perf/mxfp8-moe-fp8-mfma`. The two touch disjoint files and either can land first. The per-call timings quoted there assume the KN view from this PR.

---

AI assistance was used to investigate and prepare this change. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and measurements reported above, and is responsible for the result.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Perf] MXFP8 MoE: keep the MFMA in FP8 when MX_SCALE_BLOCK_K == 1
body:
## Motivation

The `USE_FNUZ` path added by #5658 upcasts both operands to fp32 and broadcasts both scale tiles across the full K tile, plus a `tl.trans`, before `tl.dot`. That promotes an FP8 MFMA to an FP32 one at 4x the operand footprint.

It is never a win. #5658 itself closed off the other configurations: in response to review comment [r4045560377](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5658#discussion_r4045560377) the wrapper now asserts

```python
assert quant_block_size == 32, "_moe_gemm_a8w8 hardcodes MX_PACK_DIVISOR=32"
```

and `MX_SCALE_BLOCK_K = BLOCK_K // MX_PACK_DIVISOR`, so `MX_SCALE_BLOCK_K` is always 1 on every MXFP8 MoE call. That means one scale per operand per K-step, constant across the dot.

When the scale is constant across the dot, scaling the `[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]` result is equivalent to scaling the `[*, BLOCK_K]` operands, and the operands can stay in FP8:

```python
acc += (
    tl.dot(x, w, input_precision="ieee")
    * tl.sum(a_sc, axis=1)[:, None]
    * tl.sum(b_sc, axis=1)[None, :]
)
```

This keeps the merged kernel and fixes that path. It does not revert #5658.

## Technical Details

Applied to both the main loop and the `not EVEN_K` tail. The `MX_SCALE_BLOCK_K > 1` branches are preserved byte for byte.

Those branches are unreachable today, since the assert pins `BLOCK_K = 32`. They also disagree with each other: the main loop broadcasts the weight scale on axis 2 and then transposes, while the tail broadcasts on axis 1 and does not. At most one can be correct. I have left both alone, since fixing an unreachable path is a separate concern, but reviewers should know those configurations are untested and that this PR does not try to measure them.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest op_tests/triton_tests/moe/test_moe_gemm_mxfp8.py -v
python op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_moe_gemm_mxfp8.py
```

## Test Result

MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3, idle node, Triton cache cleared between arms, best of 5 timing runs.

`E=32, N=2048, K=6144`, weights already stored K-major:

| tokens | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.99 ms | 0.30 ms |
| 64 | 0.99 ms | 0.31 ms |
| 512 | 0.99 ms | 0.33 ms |
| 2048 | 1.00 ms | 0.41 ms |

About 3.2x at decode-sized batches.

The same measurement with NK weights, where both arms pay the wrapper's per-call transpose, shows the hoist alone is worth about 0.7 ms (3.43 ms down to 2.75 ms). The remaining gap between 2.75 ms and 0.31 ms is that transpose, which the companion wrapper PR removes for callers that already store K-major.

Correctness across 13 shape and layout configurations with random E8M0 scales, including `K=96` and `K=32`, plus ragged group sizes `[0,7,64,1,100,0,84,0]` with zero-token experts: cosine >= 0.999999 against an fp32 reference in every case.

End to end on vLLM 0.30.1rc1, 8x MI325X, TP=8, `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` with real weights, with both this PR and the wrapper PR applied: decode throughput 1.68 to 10.01 tok/s, TPOT 97.65 ms, GSM8K unchanged within noise (84.00% vs 85.50% last-number, n=200, 0 errors in both arms).


## Notes for reviewers

Please add `ci:triton-300x`. The default Triton CI targets gfx950, and this path is exercised on gfx942.

The companion wrapper fix is `akii96:fix/mxfp8-moe-wrapper`. The two branches are cut from the same base and touch disjoint files, so either can land first. This one alone is numerically correct but not CUDA graph capturable, since that fix lives in the wrapper PR.

The benchmark's in-tree shapes are DSv4 oriented (`8,7168,2048` and `64,2048,7168`), so the Hy4 MoE shape above is not among them.

---

AI assistance was used to investigate and prepare this change. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and measurements reported above, and is responsible for the result.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] Add gfx1250 gluon a16w16 config for MLA q_b_proj (N=24576, K=1536)
body:
## Motivation

On gfx1250 the DSR1 FP4 decode path spends a large slice of each step in the
Triton/gluon `a16w16` GEMM. Profiling a 4-GPU DP4/EP4 server at 1k in / 4k out
showed the MLA `q_b_proj` projection (`N=24576`, `K=1536`) as the single
largest `a16w16` contributor, at roughly 11% of the decode step.

That shape has no tuned entry under
`aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx1250/gluon/gemm/gemm_a16w16/`, so the lookup falls
through to `DEFAULT.json`. The default picks a `bandwidth_bound` tile with
`BLOCK_M=32`, which is a poor fit here: at decode the M range is in the
hundreds, and the shape is compute bound, not bandwidth bound. The result is a
kernel running well below what the shape can sustain.

## Summary

Adds a single tuned config file, `GEMM-A16W16-N=24576-K=1536.json`, with
`compute_bound` entries for the `M_LEQ_128` / `M_LEQ_256` / `any` buckets
(`BLOCK_M` 128/256/256, `BLOCK_N=128`, `BLOCK_K=64`).

Config only. No kernel, dispatch, or API change, and no other shape is
affected: the file is only consulted for `N=24576, K=1536` on gfx1250.

## Performance

Isolated `a16w16` GEMM at `N=24576, K=1536`, before (DEFAULT) vs after:

| M | before (us) | after (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 99.6 | 87.0 | 1.15x |
| 256 | 114.7 | 93.9 | 1.22x |
| 512 | 148.5 | 107.3 | 1.38x |

End to end on the serving workload below, the `q_b_proj` kernel drops from
70.6 us to 31.2 us per decode step and the decode step itself goes from
39.57 ms to 37.34 ms.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, via `lm_eval` against the running server:

| Filter | n-shot | Metric | Value | Stderr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match | 0.9484 | ±0.0061 |
| strict-match | 5 | exact_match | 0.9484 | ±0.0061 |



## E2E test scenario

Base image: `rocm/fw-bringup:gfx1250-atom-20260922` (nightly).

Model `/data/Deepseek-S3_sq_a05_v2_mlperf6_1` (FP4), 4x gfx1250, DP4 attention
+ EP4 MoE, served with `atom.entrypoints.openai_server`, ISL 1024 / OSL 4096.

Accuracy was collected with `FAKE_EPLB=0` (with `FAKE_EPLB=1` the expert
routing is faked for throughput measurement and GSM8K collapses to ~1%, which
is expected and unrelated to this change):

```
pip install lm-eval[api]

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=/data/Deepseek-S3_sq_a05_v2_mlperf6_1,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```

title: [Config] Tune a8w8 bpreshuffle for Kimi-K3's KDA gate at tp4
body:
## What

Adds the 62 missing `N=3072, K=128` rows to `a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv`, plus the matching shapes in the untuned CSV.

## Why

Kimi-K3's KDA gate projection `f_b_proj` is `[M, 128] x [128, 128 * heads/tp]`. K is the KDA head dim, 128 at any tp; N is `num_local_heads * 128`, so the 96 KDA heads give **N=1536 at tp8** and **N=3072 at tp4**. Only 1536 was tuned, so tp4 misses the table on every token.

A miss here is not a slower kernel. `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` falls through to `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_ck`, whose `rowwise_heuristic_dispatch` has branches only for `K >= 512` and `K >= 192 && K % 64 == 0`. K=128 hits:

```
TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported K for heuristic dispatch: 128. Supported K greater than 192 and K % 64 == 0.")
```

so the process raises on its first token. Tuning confirms there is no CK kernel for this shape at all: every `ck` candidate reported `This GEMM is not supported!`, and every winner is cktile or flydsl.

## How

Same M grid the `N=1536` rows carry (64-step between 1024 and 4096), so padded-M lookups behave the same at both widths.

```
python3 csrc/ck_gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle/gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_untuned_gemm_kimik3.csv \
  -o aiter/configs/model_configs/a8w8_bpreshuffle_tuned_gemm_kimik3.csv \
  --mp 8 --errRatio 0.01
```

62 shapes, zero failures. 5 pick cktile at small M, 57 flydsl above -- the same split `N=1536` has.

The rows are inserted in the file's existing `(N, M, K)` order rather than letting the tuner re-sort the whole file, so the diff is 62 additions and no deletions.

## Verification

gfx950 / 256 CU, via `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` directly:

| shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tp8 `M=1..16384 N=1536 K=128` | OK | OK |
| tp4 `M=1..16384 N=3072 K=128` | **FAIL** `Unsupported K for heuristic dispatch: 128` | **OK** |

End-to-end: Kimi-K3 at `--pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 4` on MI355X x8 now serves with no framework-side GEMM override, GSM8K 5-shot over the full 1319 questions at **0.9598 flexible-extract / 0.9606 strict-match**, inside the range `recipes/Kimi-K3.md` records for this model (0.9591-0.9659 / 0.9591-0.9666).

body:
## Motivation

<!-- Explain the purpose of this PR and the goals it aims to achieve. -->
This PR adds  Triton Conv3D implementation with optimized
routing for common video-model and VAE workloads.

The public API supports FP16 and BF16 inputs, NCDHW and channels-last-3D
execution, optional bias, asymmetric stride/padding/dilation, and activations.
## Technical Details

The Conv3D router selects between the following kernel families:

- Specialized 1x1x1 Conv3D
- NCDHWc 3x3x3 Conv3D with fused activation packing
- Native NDHWC 3x3x3 Conv3D
- General im2col-free Conv3D
- Winograd F(4x4, 3x3) over the H/W axes
- Winograd with an NCDHWc input path

The implementation also adds:

- Conv3D weight-prepack and Winograd-filter caches
- Layout-preserving NCDHW and channels-last-3D behavior
- Shape-driven production routing
- Complete launch keys containing all three spatial axes
- Tuned gfx1201 launch configurations
- Configuration-table coverage for gfx1200, gfx942, and gfx950, initially
  seeded from the gfx1201 values
- Public export through `aiter.ops.triton`
- Real-model-derived benchmark shape coverage for:
  - Wan2.2 A14B VAE
  - Wan2.2 TI2V-5B VAE
  - LTX-Video 0.9.5 VAE
  - InternVideo2 and Qwen-family video patch embeddings

The benchmark reports per-layer correctness, selected Triton kernels,
kernel-only and repack-inclusive performance, aggregate throughput, and
call-count-weighted encoder/decoder totals. It exits nonzero when a requested
shape errors or fails correctness.

## Test Plan

The Conv3D test suite covers:

- FP16 and BF16

- `none`, `relu`, `relu6`, and `gelu` activations
- Asymmetric dimensions, stride, padding, and dilation
- Batched, odd-channel, and tail-masking shapes
- Winograd transform and output correctness
- Output dtype preservation
- Weight-cache reuse, invalidation, and LRU eviction
- Actual production-router dispatch
- Benchmark database, reporting, and CLI behavior
- Invalid argument and unsupported configuration handling

[ASM] [HIP] feat(fmoe): SwiGLU OAI MXFP4 FLAT 16x256 kernel for Minimax M3 (gfx950)
body:
## Summary

Same as #5794 but uses the **16x256** flat kernel instead of 16x32 for Minimax M3 decode (token ≤ 4).

- SUB_GU=256 → 3 TGs per token (vs 24 for 16x32, 6 for 16x128)
- Uses two-pass GEMM0 (gate/up split) for the larger tile
- Fewest TGs per token — best for very low concurrency (token=1)

All three variants for benchmarking:
- **16x32** (24 TGs): #5794
- **16x128** (6 TGs): #5816
- **16x256** (3 TGs): this PR

## Test plan

- [ ] `python op_tests/test_moe_2stage.py -q 6 -dim 6144,768 -e 129 -k 5 -t 1 2 4 -hip 0,0 --no-flydsl-csv`

title: [FlyDSL][gfx950] Optimize FP4 MQA prefill and decode
body:
## Summary

- replace the original FP4 MQA prefill implementation with the validated 4-wave kernel in `pa_mqa_logits_fp4_prefill.py`
- group four same-batch query rows per prefill CTA, with one row per wave and one LDS-staged KV page shared by all four waves
- use one decode kernel for every `next_n`, with cooperative head waves and no decode-to-prefill routing
- specialize internally scheduled D128 H64/H128 decode with direct global KV/scale loads and grid-aware 32- or 64-token tiles
- retain the staged-LDS decode path for external/persistent schedules and unsupported layouts
- exclude benchmark scripts, raw measurements, and experimental kernel variants from the PR

## Dependency

Depends on #5518. This branch should be rebased onto the updated `main` after #5518 merges so it inherits the corresponding page-stride, 64-bit addressing, and page128 support without duplicating that dependency's history here.

## Implementation

### Prefill

- 4 waves per CTA, one query row per wave
- four waves cooperatively load four KV pages into a single LDS stage
- LDS-resident KV is reused across the four query rows
- `32x32x64` FP4 MFMA
- next-chunk global loads overlap with computation on the final page of the current chunk
- 17,408 bytes LDS and 126 VGPRs in the measured kernel

### Decode

The decode kernel now handles all `next_n` values directly:

- head waves cooperate on the head reduction within each CTA
- internally scheduled D128 H64/H128 layouts read KV and scales directly from global memory into registers
- a 32-token, 2-wave tile is selected when the complete direct grid is at most 1024 CTAs
- larger direct grids use 64-token tiles to control launch size
- the direct path uses a 2D launch and compile-time page/chunk addressing
- scalar weight loads are selected for the larger grids where they reduce contention
- external/persistent schedules and unsupported layouts retain the staged-LDS generic path
- callers can still override `block_k` and `num_warps`

For the ordinary `next_n=1/2` direct shapes, each CTA owns one token chunk. Extra LDS stages therefore do not form a cross-chunk pipeline, and `next_n` does not itself create additional waves. Their improvement comes from exposing more grid-level parallelism with 32/64-token tiles and bypassing KV LDS staging; head waves only parallelize the head reduction.

## Performance

Measured on MI355X using median GPU kernel time. Decode results use nine paired CUDA Graph rounds with identical inputs and randomized Old/New execution order. Unless noted otherwise, rows use H64, D128, page64, and ragged context lengths averaging approximately half of `max_ctx`.

### Prefill

| Shape (`B x Q x KV`) | Old (us) | New (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AgentX trace | 781.16 | 610.38 | 1.280x |
| 1 x 512 x 64K | 249.20 | 200.74 | 1.241x |
| 1 x 1K x 64K | 473.36 | 377.41 | 1.254x |
| 1 x 2K x 32K | 451.07 | 356.27 | 1.266x |
| 1 x 1K x 128K | 910.54 | 693.36 | 1.313x |
| 4 x 256 x 16K | 121.77 | 93.07 | 1.308x |
| 8 x 128 x 8K | 69.46 | 50.87 | 1.366x |
| 1 x 4K x 4K | 98.64 | 56.60 | 1.743x |
| 1 x 8K x 8K | 372.80 | 213.22 | 1.748x |
| 2 x 8K x 8K | 745.16 | 423.80 | 1.758x |
| 1 x 8K x 32K | 1519.69 | 1206.67 | 1.259x |

### Decode

Here, Old is the original 256-token/4-wave MXFP4 decode configuration and New is the production configuration selected by the current dispatcher.

| Shape (`B x next_n x max_ctx`) | Old MXFP4 (us) | New (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 x 1 x 512 | 2.510 | 1.942 | 1.292x |
| 3 x 1 x 1K | 2.539 | 2.013 | 1.261x |
| 4 x 1 x 2K | 2.628 | 2.027 | 1.297x |
| 16 x 1 x 4352 | 3.303 | 2.392 | 1.381x |
| 8 x 1 x 8K | 2.730 | 2.416 | 1.130x |
| 1 x 1 x 32K | 2.641 | 2.056 | 1.285x |
| 1 x 1 x 64K | 2.697 | 2.270 | 1.188x |
| 1 x 1 x 128K | 3.372 | 2.384 | 1.414x |
| 2 x 2 x 512 | 2.582 | 1.961 | 1.317x |
| 2 x 1 x 768, H128 | 3.287 | 2.048 | 1.605x |
| 32 x 4 x 32K, AgentX/DSv4 MTP4 | 47.598 | 23.658 | 2.012x |

The first ten general decode rows have a 1.311x geometric-mean paired speedup. Compared with the original MXFP4 timings published in the first PR table, the current New timings are 1.432x faster geometrically. The AgentX/DSv4 MTP4 row contains 32 requests and 128 total query rows.

## Validation

- Python bytecode compilation passes
- Black formatting check passes
- Ruff lint passes
- `git diff --check` passes
- MI355X decode regression: 59 passed
- coverage includes direct, persistent, and external schedules; `next_n` 1/2/3/4/5/8; H16-H128; D128/D256; page64/page128; zero and ragged contexts; strided pages/output; and CUDA Graph replay
- all paired benchmark variants match the reference output
- prefill fixed-query and variable-query correctness sweeps pass with cosine similarity 1.0

title: feat(tune): record untuned shapes for every GEMM family, not just bf16
body:
Fixes #5267.

## Why

`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1` makes `tuned_gemm.py` append every missed bf16 shape to `bf16_untuned_gemm.csv`. That single feature is why tuning a real bf16 deployment is self-service: run the server, collect the CSV, hand it straight back to the tuner.

The fp8 per-token, block-scale and mxfp4 families have no equivalent — they log misses at INFO and write nothing — so their shape lists have to be scraped out of server logs by hand. That is also how shape-key mistakes creep in: we shipped a tuned table that never matched anything because the engine fuses two projections and dispatches `N=2688`, while the tuned rows targeted the unfused `N=2624`. A recorded shape list makes that impossible to miss.

## What

`aiter/utility/untuned_shapes.py` — `record(tuned_file, row)` appends one de-duplicated row **in the schema that family's tuner consumes**. The destination name is derived from the tuned table's own name (`*_tuned_*` → `*_untuned_*`), so a family never has to name its untuned file twice, and a merged `/tmp/aiter_configs` copy still resolves to the right destination.

Wired into the miss paths of:
- `gemm_op_a8w8.get_CKGEMM_config` (block-scale, ± preshuffle) → `M,N,K`
- `gemm_op_a8w8.get_GEMM_config_with_quant_type` (a8w8, a8w8_bpreshuffle) → `M,N,K,q_dtype_w`
- `gemm_op_a4w4.get_GEMM_config` → `M,N,K`

## Behaviour

- Same switch as before (`AITER_TUNE_GEMM=1`) — nothing new to learn; **off by default**.
- `AITER_TUNE_GEMM_DIR` overrides the destination, for read-only package directories and containers (we had to copy the file out of a container image more than once).
- Hot path cost after a shape has been seen is one set lookup; a serving run repeats its shapes, so the append happens a handful of times.
- Never raises. A read-only configs dir or a full disk must not take down inference — it logs a warning and moves on.

## Checked

Name derivation (including the merged-copy path), per-family schemas, de-duplication across repeats, disabled-by-default, and graceful degradation on an unwritable destination.

Same campaign as #5262 / #5263–#5266.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Bugfix][MLA] Mask the >2GB global_load path in mla_gluon decode (fixes gfx950 IMA)
body:
## Problem
On gfx950, serving **Kimi-K2.6** (8 heads/rank @ TP8, `kv_lora_rank=512`, bf16 KV) with vLLM crashes at decode warmup with a GPU **illegal memory access** inside the Gluon MLA decode kernel (`mla_gluon`). Its paged KV cache is far larger than 2 GB, so the wrapper sets `within_2gb=False` and KV is loaded via `global_load_to_shared` (64-bit offsets) instead of `buffer_load_to_shared`.

## Root cause
The `>2GB` `global_load_to_shared` calls (the `else` of each `if WITHIN_2GB:`) dropped the bounds `mask` that their `buffer_load_to_shared` siblings carry. A partial split block then dereferences out-of-bounds KV rows -> IMA. Additionally, `buffer_load` returns `0` for masked lanes while `global_load` leaves them undefined, so a mask alone yields **NaNs** on partial blocks -- `other=0.0` is required to match `buffer_load` semantics.

Introduced by #4474 (which added the int64 `>2GB` global_load path); still present on current `main`.

## Fix
Add `mask=<same predicate as the buffer_load sibling>, other=0.0` to all 8 `global_load_to_shared` calls in `_mla_gluon`.

## Test
Adds `test_mla_gluon_decode_over_2gb` to `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_mla.py`: it drives a >2 GB cache through the `global_load` path and asserts finiteness + bit-parity against the `<2GB` `buffer_load` reference on identical KV.

The two configs are chosen so that **every one of the 8 masked loads is executed**, keyed on `num_iter = cdiv(per_split, BLOCK_N=64)` with `per_split = max(64, ctx // NUM_KV_SPLITS)` and `NUM_KV_SPLITS = min(256 // batch, cdiv(ctx, 64))` (bh16bn64 regime):

| config | NUM_KV_SPLITS | per_split | num_iter | loads exercised |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(batch=8, ctx=777)` | 13 | 64 | 1 | prologue loads, last split is a **partial** block (mask + `other=0.0`) |
| `(batch=4, ctx=33000)` | 64 | 515 | 9 | prologue + **loop-body** loads + **epilogue** load (partial tail = 3) |

So `(4, 33000)` reaches `for i in range(num_iter - 2)` and the `if num_iter >= 2` epilogue — the paths a `num_iter == 1` config never touches.

```
pytest op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_mla.py -k test_mla_gluon_decode_over_2gb
```

The fix itself was validated on MI350 (gfx950): the >2 GB path output matches the `buffer_load` reference (`max_abs_diff=0.0`), the standalone repro goes from memory-access-fault -> clean, and **Kimi-K2.6 `-tp 8` serves** on upstream vLLM.

AI assistance was used; changes were human-reviewed.

title: fix gluon import and benchmark + tune fused_clamp_act_mul for gfx950
body:
## Motivation

On `gfx950`, `fused_clamp_act_mul` regression on Triton 3.8 at large-M prefill shapes up to 7.2%

| M | N (n_half) | Triton 3.4 | Triton 3.8 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 2048 | 34.02 us | 36.47 us | **+7.18%** |
| 8192 | 4096 | 34.44 us | 36.00 us | **+4.52%** |
| 16384 | 4096 | 62.26 us | 64.88 us | **+4.21%** |

The kernel was not tuned at M, as it was only tuned previously on row width (N). Essentially, `M=1` and `M=16384` at the same N received the same launch config. The triton path launches `grid=(M,)`, meaning one program per row, and `BLOCK_SIZE_N` is the whole row. In this case, `num_warps` is the only knob to be tuned, and past a few thousand rows, the grid alone fills the GPU. The shipped width-keyed value is tuned for small M and is too high for prefill. Decode (M <= 128) is unaffected and measures identically on both compilers.

Also, the benchmark for this kernel was not usable on main. It fails to import `_is_gluon_available()` and it crashes `rocprofv3` runs for shapes due to `rep` being hardcoded. Both issues are fixed here. 

## Technical Details

The kernel now checks the N-specialized `FUSED_CLAMP_ACT_MUL-N={N}.json` for the largest `M_GEQ_<x> <= M` before falling back to the existing `DEFAULT.json`, which is unchanged.

```
aiter/ops/triton/fusions/fused_clamp_act_mul.py                     +32 -8
op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fused_clamp_act_mul.py          +10 -2
configs/gfx950/triton/fusions/fused_clamp_act_mul/FUSED_CLAMP_ACT_MUL-N=2048.json  (new)
configs/gfx950/triton/fusions/fused_clamp_act_mul/FUSED_CLAMP_ACT_MUL-N=4096.json  (new)
```

Tuned values (gfx950, from a `num_warps` sweep of 1/2/4/8/16 per shape):

| N | shipped | M >= 4096 | M >= 16384 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 4 | **2** | **1** |
| 4096 | 8 | **4** | 4 |
| 512, 8192 | 1, 8 | unchanged (optimal) | |

### Benchmark fixes

- `is_gluon_available()` restored, as the benchmark didn't import properly. The guard now asserts properly.
- `--rep` made configurable, because the default 100 crashes `rocprofv3`. Make it an argument so that one can define the number of reps desired.

## Test Plan

- Correctness tests with pytest
- Black and Ruff checks
- `rocprofv3 --kernel-trace` runs with kernel time (10/80/10 trimmed mean)
- 23 shapes: N in {512, 2048, 4096, 8192} x M in {1, 16, 64, 128, 4096, 8192, 16384}, covering every config bucket plus decode and prefill

## Test Result

**23 shapes: 0 regressions, 5 improvements, 18 neutral.** The 5 improvements are exactly the 5 measured shapes whose `num_warps` changes; every shape whose routing is unchanged is neutral.

| M | N | main | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 2048 | 9.95 us | **9.31 us** | **-6.4%** |
| 16384 | 2048 | 36.46 us | **34.63 us** | **-5.0%** |
| 4096 | 4096 | 19.07 us | **18.44 us** | **-3.3%** |
| 8192 | 4096 | 35.89 us | **34.62 us** | **-3.5%** |
| 16384 | 4096 | 65.60 us | **63.17 us** | **-3.7%** |

**Decode unchanged.** All 13 shapes at M <= 128 are neutral
**Correctness:** `330 passed, 454 skipped, 200 warnings in 16.15s`
**Style:** `black` and `ruff==0.16.0` clean.
**Benchmark:** imports and runs; its default sweep profiles under `rocprofv3` without crashing, and `--rep 100` still reproduces the SIGSEGV on `--shape 1 512` and `--shape 16384 512`.

title: [HIP] [CK] Add relu2 (Squared ReLU) activation support to CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM
body:
## Motivation

- NemotronH's MoE layers use Squared ReLU (`relu(x)^2`) as their activation function. Tier 1 (#5689) added a standalone `relu2` kernel so aiter could compute this activation directly instead of falling back to eager PyTorch, but that PR only covered the simple elementwise case, not the fused MoE GEMM path.

- The fused MoE GEMM path (`csrc/ck_tile_gemm_moe_2stages/`) didn't support relu2 at all. 

- This PR adds real relu2 support to the fused MoE GEMM path, so NemotronH's MoE layers can run through aiter's fast CK-Tile kernels instead of falling back to a legacy path that doesn't support relu2 at all.

This is Tier 2 of a 3-PR series adding end-to-end relu2 support:

1. #5689 -- standalone aiter elementwise kernel (no dependencies)
2. This PR -- aiter CK-Tile fused MoE GEMM support for relu2 (depends
   on Tier 1)
3. vLLM AITER backend integration (depends on this PR)


## Technical Details

Root cause: `moe_dispatch` (the CK-Tile MoE GEMM's kernel-selection function) had no case for relu2's internal activation id, so relu2 calls fell through the if/else chain with no matching branch and no `return` -- genuine undefined behavior, not a crash or NaN. 

This PR adds the missing dispatch branch, along with the supporting relu2 activation functor, codegen routing, and Python-side wiring needed to reach it (`aiter.fused_moe`'s `get_2stage_cfgs` now selects the CK-Tile relu2 path instead of falling back to a legacy codegen path that has no relu2 support at all).

## Test Plan

Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-BF16`, 8x AMD Instinct MI350 (gfx950), TP=8.

- Kernel-level: `test_fmoe` (isolated CK-Tile GEMM, vs. torch-eager reference) at E=8/topk=2 across token counts {16,32,64,128,256}, and at E=512/topk=22 (NemotronH's production MoE scale).
- End-to-end: NemotronH's real checkpoint is unquantized bf16 and only reaches this fused-GEMM dispatch path when weights are quantized to fp4x2/per_1x32 at load time, so this was validated via  `--quantization mxfp4` online quantization in vLLM. Ran `vllm bench serve` (1024/1024 and 8192/1024, concurrency 128, 256 prompts) and `lm_eval` GSM8K (5-shot, n=1319) as an A/B test toggling only the `moe_dispatch` fix (identical mxfp4 quantization and hardware otherwise, fix reverted vs. applied).

## Test Result

### GPU Kernel Test

### a16w4 (weight-only mxfp4) passes cleanly at NemotronH-realistic dimensions

Testing relu2/gate-only with only the weight quantized to mxfp4 (activation left as unquantized bf16 — `AQDType=bf16`, `WQDType=fp4x2`) at `model_dim=8192, inter_dim=5120, E=8, topk=2` (NemotronH-realistic dims):

**Test configuration:**
- Shape: `model_dim=8192, inter_dim=5120, E=8, topk=2` — matches NemotronH's real hidden/intermediate dims
- Activation: `Relu2` (gate-only, `gateMode=GateMode.SEPARATED`, `use_g1u1=False`)
- Quantization: `qType=per_1x32` (mxfp4), `AQDType=bf16` (activation left unquantized), `WQDType=fp4x2` (weight quantized to mxfp4) 
- Token counts swept: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 (single forward call each, `strict_accuracy=True`)
- Metric: `logits_diff` — aiter's own `calc_diff` cosine-similarity-based distance between the CK-Tile kernel's GEMM output and an unquantized PyTorch fp32 reference computed with identical routing/weights
- Hardware: 8x AMD Instinct MI350 (gfx950), aiter editable install at commit `f42721f0e` (`amd-aiter-0.1.23.dev98+gf42721f0e`)

| token | quant config | logits_diff | result |
|------:|:---|------------:|:------:|
| 16    | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 4.686e-05 | **PASS** |
| 32    | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 3.695e-05 | **PASS** |
| 64    | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 5.848e-05 | **PASS** |
| 128   | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 2.331e-05 | **PASS** |
| 256   | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 4.611e-05 | **PASS** |

Every token count passes cleanly — `logits_diff` in the 2.3e-05–5.8e-05 range, consistent with ordinary MXFP4 weight-quantization rounding noise.

#### a16w4 passes cleanly at production MoE scale (E=512, topk=22)

Same weight-only mxfp4 configuration as above, now at NemotronH's production expert count and routing width:

**Test configuration:**
- Shape: `model_dim=8192, inter_dim=5120, E=512, topk=22` 
- Activation: `Relu2` (gate-only, `gateMode=GateMode.SEPARATED`, `use_g1u1=False`)
- Quantization: `qType=per_1x32` (mxfp4), `AQDType=bf16` (activation left unquantized), `WQDType=fp4x2` (weight quantized to mxfp4)
- Token counts swept: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 (single forward call each, `strict_accuracy=True`)
- Metric: `logits_diff` — aiter's own `calc_diff` cosine-similarity-based distance between the CK-Tile kernel's GEMM output and an unquantized PyTorch fp32 reference computed with identical routing/weights
- Hardware: 8x AMD Instinct MI350 (gfx950), aiter editable install at commit `f42721f0e` (`amd-aiter-0.1.23.dev98+gf42721f0e`), CK submodule at `1f66d862231703a0f354e5771e58573139bb6efb`

| token | quant config | logits_diff | result |
|------:|:---|------------:|:------:|
| 16    | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 6.515e-05 | **PASS** |
| 32    | a16w4 (activation unquantized) | 6.583e-05 | **PASS** |

All five token counts pass cleanly at production scale — `logits_diff` in the 6.3e-05–6.6e-05 range, the same order of magnitude as the smaller E=8/topk=2 sweep above.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] Tune gfx1201 unified attention 2d for D=512 for full attention and D=256 for Sliding Window (Gemma4 shapes) and fix D=1024 launches
body:
## Motivation

Improve unified-attention prefill on Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201) for Gemma-4-31B shapes (full attention D=512, sliding attention D=256), including fp8 KV cache, and stop `attn_2d` launch failures for head sizes that pad to 1024.

Related PRs:

- **Merged:** [#4044](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4044) documents Gemma-4 tuning on gfx950; [#4868](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4868) adds RDNA **3D** LDS guards. This change targets gfx1201 **2D**.
- **Open tuning:** [#5601](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5601) targets gfx1151; [#5650](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5650) targets gfx942 and supersedes closed [#5063](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5063); [#5432](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5432) targets gfx950.
- **Open related fix:** [#5035](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5035) is a draft gfx1201 **3D** LDS-budget fix.

## Technical Details

|---|---|---|

| 513–1024 | 1024 | LDS guard, Q ≥ 256, any dtype: BLOCK_M=32, TILE=16, 8 warps |
| > 1024, Q < 64, decode | — | unchanged existing entries |

**D=512 retune.** BLOCK_M=64 / TILE=16 / 8 warps beats the previous BLOCK_M=32
entry by ~1.3× (the earlier staged search fixed 4 warps while choosing tiles).

## Test Plan

- Routing check against the baseline table: D ≤ 128 and D > 1024 must route identically for every Q (1–299 and larger), sliding on/off, and dtype pair; heads 129–1024 must land in the band of their padded width.

## Test Result

The fp8 cases here were checked with that call fixed to pass the tensors the kernel receives (`q_tensor`/`k_tensor`/`v_tensor`); Fix is added

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] Gfx1151 blockscale tuned jsons
body:
## Motivation

Add gfx1151 (RDNA3 / Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S) tuned Triton `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE` config files for the DeepSeek-V4-Flash FP8 block-scale GEMM shapes.

On gfx1151 these blockscale GEMMs previously had no per-shape tuned config, so AITER fell back to the default kernel configuration and vLLM logged `Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config` for the uncovered shapes. This PR records measured tuned configs for the DeepSeek-V4 W8A8 block-scale shapes seen in the 1M TP=2 serving run so those shapes use tuned parameters instead of the default fallback.

This is part of the DeepSeek-V4 gfx1151/RDNA3 AITER enablement stack:

- Dependency: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52970> (officially supporting AITER Triton kernels + dsv4 on RDNA3). That PR routes the RDNA3 FP8 block-scale linear path through AITER's Triton kernels, which is what consumes these gfx1151 config files.

## Technical Details

This PR only adds tuning/config data. It does not add or modify any kernel.

All files land under:

```text
aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx1151/triton/gemm/gemm_a8w8_blockscale/
```

Added configs:

- `DEFAULT.json` (gfx1151 blockscale default entries)
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=512-K=4096.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=1536-K=4096.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=2048-K=4096.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=4096-K=256.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=4096-K=1024.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=4096-K=4096.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=4096-K=12288.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=8192-K=1024.json`
- `GEMM-A8W8_BLOCKSCALE-N=16384-K=1024.json`

Each per-shape file is keyed by `M_LEQ_*` buckets and stores the standard Triton GEMM tuning parameters (`BLOCK_SIZE_M/N/K`, `GROUP_SIZE_M`, `num_warps`, `num_stages`, `waves_per_eu`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, `cache_modifier`, `NUM_KSPLIT`, `kpack`) for the FP8 `[128, 128]` block-scale GEMM.

The `(N, K)` shapes correspond to the DeepSeek-V4-Flash W8A8 block-scale GEMMs observed on the gfx1151 1M TP=2 route.

## Test Plan

- Load the model on gfx1151 with the AITER Triton FP8 block-scale path enabled (via the vLLM dependency above) and confirm each added shape resolves to its tuned config instead of the default fallback.
- Confirm the `Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config` warnings for these `(N, K)` shapes no longer appear during startup/serving.

## Test Result

- With these configs present, the previously uncovered DeepSeek-V4 W8A8 block-scale shapes are served with tuned parameters and no longer fall back to the default kernel config.

### System-level E2E result

These configs deliver a clear end-to-end win on the DeepSeek-V4-Flash gfx1151 1M TP=2 route, exercised through the RDNA3 AITER Triton path enabled by the vLLM dependency (<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52970>). Comparing an untuned image against the tuned image on the same prompt, the tuned build cuts end-to-end latency by roughly 1.4x to 1.6x and nearly doubles output token throughput.

| Warmed follow-up E2E (s) | `52.80` | `36.94` | ~1.43x faster |

title: [Triton/Gluon] Assert SPLIT_UNMASKED_LOOP is not used with sliding window
[Triton/Gluon] Add scattered-pointer Q4_K_M MoE matvec kernel for streaming inference
body:
## Motivation

This kernel is the AITER-side primitive for a license-clean llama.cpp fork at https://github.com/ssubbotin/llama.cpp/tree/feature/moe-expert-gpu-cache, which adds a `--moe-stream-dir` flag for streaming-MoE inference: active experts live in a per-(layer, projection) VRAM LRU cache and cold experts page in from NVMe SSD on demand. Each cache slot holds one expert at an arbitrary device address; top-k routing picks K slots per token. This kernel consumes that scattered-pointer layout directly, so the engine never has to gather the K active experts into a contiguous slab before dispatch.

End-to-end this lets large MoE models run on GPUs that can't fit the full expert set in VRAM. Measured on the same fork unchanged: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Q4_K_M (17 GiB of weights) streams on a 16 GB RX 9070 XT at **21.72 tg64 tok/s**, with the OS page cache absorbing nearly all the streaming I/O after the first forward pass (cold/warm gap ≈ 13%). The same engine and the same kernel source compile and run unchanged on MI300X (gfx942), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), and Strix Halo APU (gfx1151) — see the cross-architecture table under [Numbers](#numbers).

## Summary

Adds a Triton MoE matvec kernel that consumes K active experts from K **separate device buffers**, indexed by an array of per-expert device pointers plus a `(token, slot) -> unique-expert` remap. This is the core primitive needed for **streaming-MoE inference**, where expert weights are too large to fit fully in VRAM and live as slots in a per-(layer, projection) LRU cache fed from NVMe SSD on demand.

Existing AITER MoE kernels assume a contiguous `(E, N, K)` expert tensor; the streaming case has the K active experts scattered across K cache slots whose absolute device addresses are only known at dispatch time. This kernel consumes those addresses directly, avoiding the per-dispatch device-to-device slab copy that a contiguous-tensor wrapper would require.

**Format**: GGUF Q4_K_M, the dominant on-disk MoE quantization (super-block of 256 elements, 144 bytes/block: 4-byte `dm` + 12-byte packed scales/mins + 128 bytes of nibbles). The kernel decodes the layout in registers — no host-side repack needed.

**Kernel design**: each program tiles `BLOCK_SIZE_N` output rows for one (token, slot). The Q4_K_M block-loop unrolls the 8 sub-blocks (4 il-groups × low+high nibble), avoiding both 2D gather operations and runtime nibble-position arithmetic. `BLOCK_SIZE_N` is autotuned over `{4, 8, 16, 32}`.

## Files

- ` aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/moe/moe_op_q4k_streaming.py` — Triton kernel
- ` aiter/ops/triton/moe/moe_op_q4k_streaming.py` — Python wrapper
- ` op_tests/triton_tests/moe/q4k_pack_reference.py` — pure-numpy Q4_K_M packer + reference dequant
- ` op_tests/triton_tests/moe/test_moe_q4k_streaming.py` — pytest correctness against the reference
- ` op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_moe_q4k_streaming.py` — microbenchmark over realistic MoE shapes

## Validation

The pure-numpy reference dequant is **byte-exact** against `dequantize_row_q4_K` in `libggml.so` (separate cross-validation, 23 random + edge-case blocks). The Triton kernel matches the numpy reference across 8 shapes, from synthetic edge cases to a production Qwen3-A17B-shaped expert (`n_dim_in=2048, n_dim_out=1408, K=8, n_used_per_token=8`).

## Numbers

MI300X (gfx942, ROCm 7.0.0, Triton 3.4), autotuned, fp32 in / fp32 out:

| workload                   |  ms   | GB/s | GFLOPS |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_decode | 0.104 | 632  | 2248   |
| mixtral8x7b_down_decode    | 0.127 | 520  | 1847   |
| dsv3_gate_up_decode        | 0.107 | 618  | 2196   |
| dsv3_down_decode           | 0.096 | 689  | 2449   |
| qwen35_397b_gate_up_decode | 0.030 | 477  | 1697   |
| qwen35_397b_down_decode    | 0.025 | 564  | 2006   |
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_b8     | 0.707 | 374  | 2656   |

### Cross-architecture portability

Same kernel source, same bench script, no per-arch code paths or `#ifdef`s. Triton compiles the kernel for each backend; AITER's autotuner picks `BLOCK_SIZE_N` per device. All 8 pytest correctness cases pass on each architecture.

| Workload                     | MI300X GB/s | Blackwell GB/s | RX 9070 XT GB/s | Strix Halo GB/s |
|------------------------------|------------:|---------------:|----------------:|----------------:|
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_decode   |         646 |            498 |             262 |             118 |
| mixtral8x7b_down_decode      |         519 |            436 |             240 |             106 |
| dsv3_gate_up_decode          |         627 |            520 |             270 |             118 |
| dsv3_down_decode             |         695 |            529 |             262 |             121 |
| qwen35_397b_gate_up_decode   |         484 |            364 |             240 |             110 |
| qwen35_397b_down_decode      |         566 |            460 |             223 |             109 |
| mixtral8x7b_gate_up_b8       |         375 |            295 |             130 |              70 |

Peaks: 695 / 529 / 270 / 121 GB/s. Backends, in order: ROCm 7.0.0 + Triton 3.4 (MI300X), CUDA 13.0 + Triton 3.6 (Blackwell), ROCm 7.2.2 + Triton 3.6 (RX 9070 XT), TheRock ROCm 7.13.0a + Triton 3.6 (Strix Halo).

The kernel is decode-style memory-bound. Further gains (toward HBM3 peak) would come from wider weight loads (uint32-packed nibbles) and wave-level reduction; left as a follow-up so this change stays focused on the scattered-pointer primitive.

## Test plan

- [x] ` python -m pytest op_tests/triton_tests/moe/test_moe_q4k_streaming.py` — 8/8 pass on MI300X (gfx942), RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), and Strix Halo (gfx1151)
- [x] ` python op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_moe_q4k_streaming.py` — runs across all reference workloads on all four backends
- [x] Numpy reference byte-exact vs ` libggml.so:dequantize_row_q4_K`

title: [Triton/Gluon] [ASM] [HIP] Mha v4: adds bf16 sparse, LSE support, KV varlen, fixes, etc
body: ⚠️ These MHA kernels are mainly tested & intended for Diffusion Inference workloads. However, mha_v4 gfx950 bf16 is virtually as accurate as mha_v3 at +100 TFlops 👌 ## Motivation Add log-sum-exp output to MHA v4 gfx950 kernels (only dense variants now), so it can run under ring / context parallelism, which merges per-rank partials via LSE. Also extends block-sparse to the BF16 recipes, canonicalizes the MXFP4 rows, and improves K/V quantization accuracy. ## Technical Details Kernels - New BF16 and BF16FP8 sorted-sparse kernels. - Dense LSE epilogue on all ten hd128 recipes, gated at runtime on `s_lse`. - `f8f6`, `f6f4` and `mxfp4` sparse rows moved to FP6-P V, matching their dense siblings. - Dense `mxfp4` claims the canonical FP6-P V order; the duplicate `f4f4` row is disabled. Host - bugfix: per-channel V amax clamped so empty heads cannot quantize to NaN. - Optional `lse` output on `mha_v4` / `mha_v4_packed`, plumbed through `asm_mha_v4_fwd.cu`. + ABI unchanged: `ptr_lse` / `s_lse` / `s_lse_Hs` were already reserved in the kernarg. - `_LSE_CAPABLE_QV` gates the supported format pairs; sorted-sparse still raises. - K mean is subtracted before quantizing (K-smoothing), fused into the MX quantizer kernels. - Dense MHA v4 accepts per-batch key lengths (ragged `seqlen_k`). Minor - Retired `MXFP4 Q/K + FP8 V` and the deprecated `mha_v4_mxfp8` alias. - `bench_sage.py`: improve input distributions, diffusion-calibrated default, BF16 sparse modes. - Split the block-sparse cases into `op_tests/test_mha_v4_sparse.py`. ## Test Plan 1. Run the complete MHA v4 test suite on MI355X/gfx950. 2. Per-recipe dense and sparse validation against Torch; full-LUT sparse bit-exact vs dense. 3. Compare LSE against float32 `torch.logsumexp` for every capable format pair. 4. Compare O bitwise, LSE off vs on and against the previous code objects. 5. Interleaved A/B throughput, 12 rounds per variant on one idle GPU. ## Test Result 1. 330 passed, 1 skipped in test_mha_v4.py + test_mha_v4_sparse.py on MI355X/gfx950. 2. Dense validation passes 10/10 recipes; unchanged sparse objects are byte-identical. 3. LSE vs float32: bf16 max_abs 7.2e-4; quantized rows |mean_off| <= 0.046. 4. O bitwise unchanged vs the previous objects (40/40 cases); dense throughput at parity 5. black --check and ruff on PR-touched Python files: passed. Previous PRs: #5335, #5005, #4967, #4627

title: [Triton/Gluon] gfx942: dtype-split large-prefill attn_2d entries for head 256/512 (Gemma-4)
body:
## Summary

Adds four `attn_2d` entries to the gfx942 unified-attention table so large prefill on head-256/512 layers (Gemma-4-31B: 10 full-attention layers at head 512, sliding layers at head 256) stops running on the decode-era `BLOCK_M=16` configs. Continues and supersedes the config side of #5063, informed by a side-by-side with #5649.

```json
"D_GEQ_512.Q_GEQ_1024.DT_fp8_fp8":  {"BLOCK_M": 128, "num_warps": 8, "num_stages": 2, "waves_per_eu": 2, "TILE_SIZE_MIN": 16, "TILE_SIZE_MAX": 16},
"D_GEQ_512.Q_GEQ_1024.DT_bf16_bf16": {"BLOCK_M": 64, "num_warps": 8, "num_stages": 2, "waves_per_eu": 2, "TILE_SIZE_MIN": 16, "TILE_SIZE_MAX": 16},
"D_GEQ_256.Q_GEQ_1024.DT_fp8_fp8":  {"BLOCK_M": 64, "num_warps": 2, "num_stages": 2, "waves_per_eu": 2, "TILE_SIZE_MIN": 16, "TILE_SIZE_MAX": 16},
"D_GEQ_256.Q_GEQ_1024.DT_bf16_bf16": {"BLOCK_M": 64, "num_warps": 4, "num_stages": 2, "waves_per_eu": 2, "TILE_SIZE_MIN": 16, "TILE_SIZE_MAX": 16}
```

## Why dtype-split

The two prior attempts at this used dtype-agnostic composite keys. Measured on MI325X (isolated kernel bench, same kernel body for every arm — only `select_2d_config`'s return is swapped; Gemma-4 per-rank shapes 32q/4kv, page 64, 16k tokens, median `do_bench`):

**fp8 q+kv (D=512, 16k tokens):**

| arm | ms | regs / spills |
|---|---|---|
| table `D_GEQ_512.DT_fp8_fp8` (M16/T32/w4) | 43.6 | 211 / 0 |
| #5649 `D_GEQ_512.Q_GEQ_256` (M64/T16/w4) | 25.7 | 256 / 0 |
| **new fp8 entry (M128/T16/w8)** | **18.9** | 238 / 0 |

**bf16 (D=512, 16k tokens):**

| arm | ms |
|---|---|
| table `D_GEQ_512` (M16/T16/w4) | 69.9 |
| #5649 entry applied to bf16 (M64/T16/w4) | **93.0 — regression** (CI triton 3.8.0) |
| **new bf16 entry (M64/T16/w8)** | **38.8** |

The fp8-tuned warp count regresses bf16, and BLOCK_M 128 at bf16 overflows the 64KB LDS (compile error, required 131072). So the entries are split on `DT`.

**D=256 sliding-window prefill (SW=1024, 16k tokens):**

| dtype | table (M16/T32/w4) | new entry |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 3.32 | **1.21** (M64/T16/w2) |
| bf16 | 4.49 | **1.84** (M64/T16/w4) |

## Why Q_GEQ_1024

Measured crossover vs the D-only entries is between 512 and 1024 tokens (at Q=512 the D-only entries still win on both dtypes; at Q=1024 the composites win). Binding at 256 (as #5649 does) gives the new configs sub-1k-token prefills where they slightly lose; binding at 1024 leaves those on the existing entries.

## Pre-shuffled KV note

The pre-shuffled A8W8 path pins `TILE_SIZE = block_size` after lookup (`unified_attention.py`, `_unified_attention_2d_triton`). With block_size 64 at head 512, M64/T64 needs 69632B of LDS — over the 65536B limit — so this entry must not be used as-is there; measured M16/T64 (the current effective config for that path) compiles and runs. The new keys are dtype-scoped to plain fp8/bf16 KV; the pre-shuffled path should get its own entry after a dedicated tuning pass (not attempted here).

## Verification

- Isolated kernel bench on MI325X, both triton 3.7.1 (vllm-openai-rocm v0.28.0 image) and **3.8.0 (aiter CI pin, installed from pypi.amd.com)**: numbers above are from 3.8.0; 3.7.1 agrees within ~5%.
- Register/spill stats via kernel `n_regs`/`n_spills`: every new entry compiles with 0 spills (M128/w8 fp8: 238 regs, LDS exactly 65536B).
- Lookup regression tests: `op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_unified_attention_config.py` asserts the matched key and BLOCK_M for all 18 cases (both dtypes × both head tiers × decode controls × Q=1023/1024 boundary), run against the actual `_lookup`/`_axis_values` from this branch — 18/18 pass.
- Output equivalence between arms verified in-bench (max abs diff at fp8 = 1 quant step of the synthetic input scale; 0 at bf16).

## Pre-shuffled KV (follow-up commit)

The SHUF axis was added to the schema so pre-shuffled A8W8 prefill (where the wrapper pins `TILE_SIZE = block_size` post-lookup) gets LDS-safe, separately tuned entries: head 512 `M32/w4/s1` (42.2 → 28.6 ms) and head 256 `M128/w8/s2` (16.6 → 9.1 ms), both fp8, MI325X. Six shuffled lookup cases cover Copilot's ask; 24/24 total pass.

title: [HIP] Guard GroupNorm vectorization at channel boundaries
body:
## Summary

- Require the per-channel element count to be divisible by four before enabling GroupNorm vectorization.
- Keep Python workspace sizing consistent with the HIP launch configuration.
- Make GroupNorm correctness failures fatal and report the worst mismatch.
- Add a regression shape where the group span is divisible by four but the channel span is not.

## Motivation

The vectorized output path applies the affine parameters selected for the vector's first element to all four values. Therefore, a vector must never cross a channel boundary.

The previous condition checked whether the complete group span was divisible by four. That could enable vectorization when an individual channel had an incompatible element count.

This is a general correctness fix and is not specific to gfx908.

## Testing

Tested on AMD Instinct MI100 (`gfx908`) with:

- FP16
- BF16
- FP32
- small tensors
- multi-batch odd spatial dimensions
- aligned channel spans
- the odd `32769` channel-span regression case

All 12 dtype/shape combinations passed with zero tolerance violations.

`git diff --check` also passes.

title: [CustomAllreduce] Re-take the expandable_segments decision at capture time
body:
`CustomAllreduce` refuses its registered (copy-free) CUDA-graph capture path while PyTorch `expandable_segments` is on, because VMM-backed pointers cannot be exported with `hipIpcGetMemHandle` (#4174). It then stages every all-reduce input through a device-to-device copy (`__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer`) into the pre-registered input pool.

That veto is decided **once, in `__init__`**:

```python
if not self._use_vmm and _expandable_segments_enabled():
    ...
    enable_register_for_capturing = False
self.enable_register_for_capturing = enable_register_for_capturing
```

A host that wants the registered path has one clean way to get it: keep expandable segments for weights, KV cache and eager allocations, and turn them off only for the duration of graph capture, so the graph pool's activations are ordinary `hipMalloc` memory and *are* exportable. Today that does nothing. By the time `capture()` runs the veto has already latched, and the copy-in path is taken regardless of what the allocator is doing.

## The fix

- Record what the caller asked for (`_register_for_capturing_requested`) *before* the `expandable_segments` veto.
- In `capture()`, re-evaluate the veto against the **live** allocator state. `_expandable_segments_enabled()` already reads the allocator snapshot, so no new plumbing. If expandable segments are off at that point, use the registered path for this capture.
- Restore the flag in `capture()`'s `finally`, so the decision is scoped to the capture window and never leaks into eager calls.
- The gfx1250 veto is architectural (peers would dereference unregistered pointers on replay) and is deliberately **not** re-evaluated. The VMM transport is unaffected.
- Add a class-level marker, `CustomAllreduce.defers_capture_registration = True`, so hosts can feature-detect this instead of inferring it from a version number. vLLM's side (vllm-project/vllm#57481) probes for it and stays inert without it.

Behaviour with the default configuration is unchanged. If expandable segments are on at `__init__` and still on at capture, the copy-in path is used exactly as before. If they are off at `__init__`, nothing is vetoed in the first place. Disabled communicators (unsupported world size, multi-node group, no `custom_ar` library) are still entered by `graph_capture()`. Both new attributes are set before `__init__` can return early, so `capture()` keeps working there. If `flush_graph_buffers` raises, the flag is still restored.

The re-check only ever *relaxes* the veto, and only for a caller that asked for the registered path. **Precondition for hosts:** every all-reduce input captured in the window must be allocated inside it. A tensor allocated earlier, while expandable segments were on, is still VMM-backed and cannot be IPC-exported. That is the case when the graph pool's activations feed the all-reduces, which is what a graph-capturing host normally does. The precondition is documented on `defers_capture_registration`.

## Impact

Measured with vLLM on 8x MI355X, Kimi-K3 decode (conc 1, 131k context, MTP K=6), rank 0, 4 captured passes. The host turns expandable segments off for capture (vllm-project/vllm#57481). The aiter side was applied as a runtime overlay carrying the same `capture()` logic as this PR:

| | host toggle only | host toggle + this change |
|---|---|---|
| `__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer` launches | 1396 | **236** |
| kernels launched | 12188 | **11028** |
| KDA layer (main stream) | 338.6 us | **263.3 us** |
| MLA layer (main stream) | 591.9 us | **475.8 us** |

The drop is **exactly -1160 copies = 792 two-stage + 368 one-stage all-reduce calls**, i.e. one staging copy per collective, all gone. To confirm a host is getting the registered path, look for `expandable_segments is off at capture time; using the registered custom-allreduce capture path` (logged at INFO on each capture). The `__init__` warning still fires when expandable segments are on at construction. It now says the decision is re-checked at capture instead of saying it forces copy-in.

## Test plan

New `op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_custom_allreduce_capture_registration.py`. Neither existing test covers both axes: `test_init_dist_env.py` sets expandable segments but captures no graph, and `test_custom_allreduce.py` captures a graph but never touches the allocator config. Each rank starts with `expandable_segments:True`, builds the communicator, then captures one all-reduce with and without the host toggle. It asserts:

- the `__init__` veto still fires (`enable_register_for_capturing is False` after construction);
- inside `capture()` the registered path is on if and only if the host turned expandable segments off;
- the decision does not leak out of `capture()`;
- every rank picked the same path. The registered/unregistered choice changes the kernel algorithm and the graph-buffer count, so a split across ranks is a collective mismatch, not a local inefficiency;
- the replayed graph produces the correct sum.

On platforms where the veto cannot happen (gfx1250, the VMM transport, or a build that ignores
`expandable_segments`), the flag assertions are skipped with a warning and only the result is
checked, as `test_init_dist_env.py` does. `-t 3` covers a disabled communicator.

```
for tp in 2 3 4 8; do python3 op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_custom_allreduce_capture_registration.py -t $tp; done
python3 op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_custom_allreduce.py
python3 op_tests/multigpu_tests/test_init_dist_env.py
```

## Test result

8x MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3df4ae15` (torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0).
aiter was built from source. The control is upstream `main` at 1ec3cf48e, the base of this PR.

**New test**

| | TP=2 | TP=3 (disabled comm) | TP=4 | TP=8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, `toggle=False` | pass (copy-in) | pass | pass (copy-in) | pass (copy-in) |
| this PR, `toggle=True` | **pass (registered)** | pass | **pass (registered)** | **pass (registered)** |
| `main`, `toggle=True` | FAIL: stays on copy-in | – | FAIL | FAIL |

On `main`, `toggle=True` fails at every TP size with `expected enable_register_for_capturing=True inside capture(), saw False`, so the test catches the latched veto. TP=3 failed with `AttributeError: 'CustomAllreduce' object has no attribute 'enable_register_for_capturing'` on an earlier revision of this PR that set the attributes after `__init__`'s early returns. That is why they are now set first.

**Existing tests**

- `test_init_dist_env.py`: passes, all three modes (default / expandable / raw_override), in 6 of 8 runs across this PR and `main`. Two runs on this PR's tree hung, each time after other multi-GPU tests had run in the same container. Both hangs were in torch's rendezvous (`init_process_group` -> `_create_c10d_store`), which runs before any `CustomAllreduce` is constructed, so they cannot involve this change. The same sequence passed on both trees when repeated, and I could not pin down the cause.
- `test_custom_allreduce.py`: fails **identically on this PR and on `main`** in this environment, with `AttributeError: 'DataFrame' object has no attribute 'host_time_sum'`. The profiler returns no events, and the error is raised in `perftest`'s profiler post-processing (`aiter/test_common.py`), not in an all-reduce check. With expandable segments off, which is that test's default, this change is a no-op anyway: nothing is vetoed, so there is nothing to re-take.

title: [HIP] [Kernel] Fix group quant dispatch for hidden sizes in (4096, 6144]
body:
## Problem

`rmsnorm_quant` and `add_rmsnorm_quant` abort for any group quant whose `group_size` is not a multiple of 24 when `4096 < n <= 6144`.

The dispatch selects `thread_data_size` from `n`, then `ADD_RMSNORM_QUANT_KERNEL_IMPL_` asserts `group_size % thread_data_size == 0`. That band uses `thread_data_size = 24`, so `group_size = 32` -- `QuantType.per_1x32`, i.e. both MXFP4 and MXFP8 -- fails:

```
[AITER] csrc/kernels/rmsnorm_quant_kernels.cu:447 operator() group_size not support: 32
```

This is not a feature request: the existing `per_1x32` test path hits it on `main`.

```
python op_tests/test_rmsnorm2dFusedAddQuant.py --mode 8 -n 5120 -m 8 --quant_dtype fp4x2
```

It went unnoticed because the default `-n` sweep is `[1024, 2048, 3584, 4096, 8192]`, which skips the band entirely.

## Fix

The `n <= 8192` branch already solves this problem: when `group_size != 0` it deliberately avoids `thread_data_size = 32` and selects `(512, 16)` or `(1024, 8)` by CU count. This applies the same rule to the `(4096, 6144]` band, reusing those same instantiations -- both cover `n`, and 32 is a multiple of 16 and of 8.

Strictly additive: `group_size == 0` and any multiple of 24 keep the existing `(256, 24)` config, so no currently-working call changes kernel.

## Validation

gfx950 / MI355X. Before the fix both shapes abort; after, the existing mode-8 numerical check against the torch reference passes (test tolerance is `1e-2`):

|   m |    n | quant_dtype | hip err | hip bw(GB/s) |
|----:|-----:|:------------|--------:|-------------:|
|   8 | 5120 | fp4x2       | 0.00486 |         22.4 |
| 256 | 5120 | fp4x2       | 0.00668 |        600.9 |
|   8 | 6144 | fp4x2       | 0.00566 |         25.9 |
| 256 | 6144 | fp4x2       | 0.00636 |        448.8 |

MXFP8 was checked separately: at hidden 5120, `add_rmsnorm_quant` with `group_size=32` and a 1-byte E8M0 scale now produces FP8 E4M3 values plus per-32 E8M0 scales that agree with a reference MX quantizer on 99.7% of block scales, with dequantized values within one E4M3 ULP and the residual output bit-exact. `group_size = 0` was re-checked as unchanged.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has `hidden_size = 5120`, so today none of its dense MXFP8 activations can use the fused norm+quant path. Measured on MI355X, folding the MX quant into the norm is 1.49x at M=8 and 1.77x at M=256 versus `add_rmsnorm` followed by a separate MX quant launch (2.2us and 4.1us saved per call, graph-replay latency with the replay floor amortized over 64 copies), and removes one kernel launch per occurrence.
