title: [Triton/Gluon] [Perf] Shallow-copy GEMM configs instead of deep-copying them
body:
`get_gemm_config()` returns `copy.deepcopy(config)` of a bucket dict it took
from an `lru_cache`. The copy is load-bearing — callers mutate what they get
back, `compute_splitk_params()` in place and the gluon paths via
`config.pop("kernel_type")` — but every value in a GEMM bucket is a scalar, so
`dict(entry)` isolates the cached entry identically. `copy.deepcopy` takes its
atomic fast path for `int`/`str`/`bool`/`None`, so both copies hand the kernel
the *same* value objects: nothing downstream can observe the difference.

This is the rule the repo already states in `configs/CLAUDE.md` and
`.github/instructions/aiter-ops-triton.instructions.md` — "`dict(...)` for flat
entries, `copy.deepcopy` for nested ones" — and the one `get_conv_config()`
already follows, its docstring saying it is modeled on `get_gemm_config()` and
that "a deep copy only adds hot-path overhead". `get_gemm_config()` is the
shared loader for ~28 Triton GEMM kernels and runs once per launch.

## Micro

gfx950 MI355X, torch 2.12.0+git6bbd260, `d483dbf` against `d483dbf` + this
change, single tenant on an otherwise idle host. Host wall-clock on the dispatch
path, calls issued back to back without syncing; `do_bench` reports kernel time
and is blind to this. Four interleaved pairs with the order alternated, pair 0
discarded, median of the other three; 6 shapes × 4000 iterations × 9 repeats.
The trailing-`synchronize()` drain stayed at 0.005–0.014 µs/call across all 72
kept points, so the host is what was timed.

| | base | patched | | per-shape range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get_gemm_config()` alone | 2.46 µs | 0.12 µs | **−95.1 %** | 92.3–95.2 % |
| `gemm_a16w16()` dispatch | 27.35 µs | 24.90 µs | **−8.7 %** | 8.3–9.9 % |
| `gemm_afp4wfp4()` dispatch | 37.42 µs | 33.87 µs | **−9.1 %** | 8.0–9.7 % |

The two GEMM families agree because each pays exactly one copy per launch: about
2.4 µs, which is 9 % of their host dispatch. The outlier shape in the first row
is M=23, which lands in a bucket whose lookup is itself slower.

## Engine startup

The one place the change has a measurable effect under vLLM's defaults. Timing
the function itself across a full `LLM()` init of gpt-oss-120b, rather than
looking for it in wall-clock startup, which weight I/O dominates:

| | calls | time in `get_gemm_config` |
|---|---|---|
| base | 51 156 | 408.8 / 397.8 ms |
| patched | 51 156 | 55.5 / 56.8 ms |

Two repeats each; the call count is identical by construction. About 345 ms per
engine start, 0.4–0.5 % of init.

## What reaches this code

Counted by instrumenting `get_gemm_config` inside the aiter tree, so
tensor-parallel workers are included, rather than inferred from config files:

| model | calls | family |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b | 51 156 at startup, 0 per decode step | `GEMM-A16W16` |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct | 4 200 at startup, 0 per decode step | `BATCHED_GEMM-A16WFP4` |
| Qwen3-14B-FP8, MiniMax-M2.7 | 0 | — |

Under vLLM's default HIP-graph path a decode step makes no calls at all;
`--enforce-eager` on gpt-oss gives 108 per step. So the win lands on startup,
prefill, graph capture, eager execution, tuning sweeps and callers outside vLLM,
and **cannot** move graph-mode decode throughput.

## End to end

`vllm bench serve`, TP=1, ISL 2000 / OSL 150, 60 prompts, concurrency 24,
interleaved pairs with the order alternated and pair 0 discarded. Included to
show nothing regresses; by the counts above it cannot show a gain.

**Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct**, 5 kept pairs, with an **A/A control** — the
base build against a second copy of itself, given the same separate cache roots
the real pair gets:

| | per-pair Δ tok/s | band |
|---|---|---|
| base vs patched | −3.46 −4.10 +0.76 −3.72 +0.44 | −4.1 … +0.8 % |
| base vs base (A/A) | −0.99 +0.91 +3.08 +5.02 | −1.0 … +5.0 % |

Throughput on this model is bimodal: 5 of 18 runs land near 21 500 tok/s instead
of 22 400. Three are the patched arm — and **two are an unpatched arm in the A/A
control**, which is what rules the patch out. The bands are the same width, so
this harness cannot resolve anything below about 5 % here.

TTFT does resolve, and it is the metric prefill lives in:

| | base | patched | Δ | spreads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 475.2 | 475.7 | +0.10 % | 0.9 % / 0.5 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 483.0 | 482.4 | −0.12 % | 0.6 % / 0.6 % |

**gpt-oss-120b**, 5 converged pairs (its first two are warmup — one base run came
in at 6 838 tok/s): total 28 800 → 28 866 tok/s (+0.23 %, base spread 5.1 %),
mean TPOT 7.46 → 7.43 ms, mean TTFT 461.7 → 456.9 ms.

## Accuracy

`lm_eval` GSM8K, 5-shot greedy, all 1319 items, `max_model_len=4096`,
`max_gen_toks=256`, `enable_prefix_caching=False`, `seed=1234`. `base2` is a
second run of the **unpatched** build, so its delta is the harness's noise floor.

| model | strict base | patched | Δ patch | Δ base-repeat | stderr | identical text base→patched | base→base |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b | 0.2699 | 0.2714 | +0.0015 | +0.0197 | ±0.0122 | 2.0 % | 1.5 % |
| Qwen3-Next-80B (0 calls) | 0.8105 | 0.8249 | +0.0144 | +0.0083 | ±0.0108 | 37.1 % | 33.7 % |

On the affected model a repeat of the unpatched build moves the score 13× further
than the patch does, and in both models the patched arm reproduces base's text at
least as often as base reproduces its own. Same-verdict rate is 71.9 % and 94.6 %.
gpt-oss's absolute score is low because `strict-match` does not fit its output
format; only the within-model comparison is read here.

No measurable accuracy change on GSM8K, within the base-repeat noise floor. GSM8K
exercises one shape of one path and says nothing about long context, sampling or
multi-turn.

The end-to-end and GSM8K arms also carried two lazy-logging conversions that have
since been split out of this PR. Neither reaches those call sites in any material
number — gpt-oss never calls them, Kimi-Linear calls `dynamic_mxfp4_quant` 14
times in a whole run — so those measurements stand for the change as it ships.

## Tests

`op_tests/triton_tests/gemm/basic/test_gemm_a16w16.py` 360 passed / 648 skipped
and `test_gemm_afp4wfp4.py` 234 passed / 290 skipped, identical on both arms.

`op_tests/triton_tests/test_config_copy_contract.py` is new, and covers more than
this change. Four loaders return `dict(entry)` of an `lru_cache`d object —
`get_gemm_config`, `get_conv_config`, `get_mhc_config`, `get_mhc_post_config` —
and nothing tested that contract for any of them. A nested value in any of their
tables would be shared between the cache and the caller, and a caller mutating it
in place would poison every later lookup of that shape, with no exception raised.

Three layers: the shipped gemm, conv and mhc tables are walked for **every**
architecture rather than the one running the test; the loaders are driven to
check the isolation itself, since reading the tables alone would still pass if a
loader returned the cached object; and an inventory test fails when a new
`dict(entry)` loader appears without coverage, so this tracks the source instead
of freezing at the set that exists today.

It was run against six deliberately wrong trees, each of which takes down a
different subset — a nested value in a gemm bucket, in a conv exact-shape pin and
in an mhc bucket; a typo'd bucket key the walk does not recognise; a loader that
hands back the cached object (5 of 9); and a new uncovered shallow-copy loader.
All nine pass on the shipped tree.

It lives under `op_tests/triton_tests/` because that is what CI actually
collects — the Triton job pytest-runs that directory recursively on any PR
touching `aiter/ops/triton/**`, which this PR does.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Attention] Add overflow-guarded per-call int32 varlen strides
body:
## Summary

AITER's Triton variable-length attention currently selects 32- vs 64-bit stride arithmetic through process-global state. This PR adds a **per-call** opt-in so a caller can request 32-bit addressing when the complete launch is safe, without changing other concurrent attention calls.

`prefer_int32_strides=True` uses the int32 specialization only when the checked tensor layout and launch geometry fit safely in int32. Otherwise the existing int64 path is used or, for unsupported metadata/implementations, the opt-in is rejected explicitly.

Defaults are unchanged.

## Safety boundary

The opt-in is currently limited to BF16 inference, matching the qualified use case. FP16/FP32 keep the existing int64 dispatch, as does training.

The guard covers:

- Q/K/V, output and LSE storage offsets and strides
- production tile sizes
- padded and one-past tile coordinates
- sequence-coordinate and sliding-window arithmetic
- flattened launch-grid bounds
- 1D contiguous cumulative-length metadata

Unsupported implementations such as Gluon/DAO do not silently ignore the request.

## Validation

The current test suite runs the new branch in the normal Triton attention pytest path. On MI300X/gfx942, **307 tests pass** across the bounds/configuration suite and GPU dispatch/parity cases. The GPU cases cover output and LSE, graph replay, causal/windowed attention, GQA, strided views, head padding and independent FP32 references. FP16/FP32 fallback is also checked.

For the long MiniMax H3 attention shape that motivated this work, the isolated primitive improved from **134.90 ms to 84.80 ms (1.59x)**.

With the companion SGLang adapter (#39249), a matched 8x MI300X MiniMax H3 run with Cache-DiT off improved full generation time from **208.17 s to 142.12 s**, or **46.48% more serial clips/hour**. The three measured decoded audio/video outputs were identical between the two arms.

Short attention shapes can regress, so this PR does not enable the option by default or claim a universal speedup.

## Review question

The main maintainer question is whether the per-call API and its safety/fallback boundary are the right abstraction for Triton varlen attention. The implementation does not change the attention algorithm or remove overflow protection.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [gfx950] Fix ff_a16w16_fused M<=8 launch failure, add tuned configs
body:
## Motivation

Two problems with the gfx950 configs for `ff_a16w16_fused_gated` / `ff_a16w16_fused_ungated`.

**A launch failure at 4 < M <= 8.** `M_LEQ_8` is the only bucket in `gfx950-FF-A16W16-fused.json` with `num_stages=2`, and `BLOCK_SIZE_N=256` with `BLOCK_SIZE_K=256` double-buffered does not fit in LDS on gfx950. Every call in that range raises at launch, on any shape, tuned or not.

**Small batch is served by a large-M tile.** The remaining buckets use `BLOCK_SIZE_M=64` with `num_stages=1`, so at M=8-32 the kernel runs a 64-row tile over a handful of real rows with no software pipeline. This kernel exists to be the fast path at small batch (#778: "only outperforms the two-kernel implementation when M < 128"), so that is the regime that matters for it.

## Technical Details

**1. `M_LEQ_8` bucket.**

```
triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory,
Required: 278464, Hardware limit: 163840
```

Reproduce on current `main`, gfx950 — any shape, M=8:

```python
from aiter.ops.triton.gemm.feed_forward.ff_a16w16_fused_gated import ff_a16w16_fused_gated
# M=8, hidden=3072, intermediate=8192  ->  OutOfResources at launch
```

Changed to `BLOCK_SIZE_M=32, BN=128, BK=256, num_stages=2`. It fits, and it is faster than simply dropping to `num_stages=1`, measured at M=8 on shapes with no specialized config (ms, lower is better):

| untuned shape | `BN256 BK256 ns2` (current) | `ns1` | `BN128 BK256 ns2` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| H=3072, I=8192 | crash | 0.0968 | **0.0753** |
| H=1024, I=4096 | crash | 0.0366 | **0.0269** |

**2. Seven per-`(N,K)` specialized configs.** Re-tuned with `num_stages` 2/3 re-enabled. `num_stages=1` dates from #2940, which worked around the LLVM `87717bf9` SIInsertWaitcnts crash of Apr 2026; that is fixed in the current LLVM pin (`b010a18d`), verified by re-running the shapes that used to crash with `num_stages=2/3`.

An LDS constraint shapes the search: `BK=256` with `num_stages>=2` needs ~328 KB at `BM>=32` and will not compile, so `BK<=128` is required whenever `ns>=2` at those block sizes.

Note on dimensions: the kernel's `(M, N, K)` are not the FF dimensions. Batch is `M`, `K = hidden`, and `N = 2 x intermediate` (gate and up halves stored concatenated). Filenames use the kernel `N, K`.

Also adds `utils/_triton/tunning/ut_ff_a16w16_fused_gated.py`. It pops `NUM_KSPLIT`: this kernel takes no such parameter, because its down-projection is already split over `pid_n` and recombined with `tl.atomic_add`, so the split count is not selectable.

## Test Plan

1. **M=8 regression.** Called through the default path (`config=None`) at M=8 on both tuned and untuned shapes, confirming the launch failure is gone and untuned shapes pick up the fixed default bucket.
2. **Correctness.** Every config checked against an fp32 reference, `((x @ w1[:I].T) * (x @ w1[I:].T)).bf16().f32() @ w2`, gate rel <= 6e-2. The tolerance is not slack: the kernel accumulates with `tl.atomic_add(..., sem="relaxed")`, so summation order varies per run and bf16 addition is not associative. Results are correct but not bit-reproducible by construction.
3. **Performance.** Three-way sweep on `main` — current shipped config vs this PR vs the unfused `ff_a16w16_gated` path — over 3 shapes x M in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}, `triton.testing.do_bench`.
4. **Resolution check.** Verified `get_gemm_config` picks up the specialized files and that shapes without one fall back to the default with `is_tuned=False`.

## Test Result

M=8, default path, previously crashing:

| shape | specialized config? | result |
|---|---|---|
| H=3072, I=8192 | no | OK (was OutOfResources) |
| H=1280, I=8192 | yes | OK (was OutOfResources) |
| H=8192, I=28672 | no | OK (was OutOfResources) |

Speedup over the currently shipped config (M=8 omitted: the baseline cannot run):

| shape (H x I) | M=4 | M=16 | M=32 | M=64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 x 8192 | 1.58x | 1.81x | 1.79x | 1.49x |
| 4096 x 14336 | 1.39x | 1.39x | 1.37x | 1.35x |

All within the correctness gate; shapes without a specialized config are unaffected apart from the `M_LEQ_8` fix.

**Scope of the claim.** These numbers compare the fused kernel against its own shipped config. They are not a claim that the fused kernel is the right choice at every one of these points — for `4096 x 14336` the unfused two-GEMM path is still faster at M=4-32 (fused/unfused 0.68-0.83x), and only wins at M=64 (1.26x). Choosing between the two kernels is an API-level routing question, not something a config can express. This PR makes the fused kernel faster whenever it is the one being called.

**Not included:** a config for `8192 x 28672`. Re-tuning it measured 0.96-1.06x versus the shipped config, i.e. neutral, so it does not earn a specialized file. It still benefits from the `M_LEQ_8` fix through the default bucket.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Unified attention: opt-in prefill configs for head sizes 129+
body:
## Motivation

This PR covers a Triton regression raised in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/4137: Unified attention prefill regressed on gfx950 for head sizes 129 and above. On the Qwen3.5-397B debug shape the kernel went from about 4ms on Triton 3.6 to 16ms on 3.7 and 12ms on 3.8. This is due to three separate problems:

**Register pressure.** At `BLOCK_M=128` a head size in 129-255 pads to a 256-element accumulator, and the kernel needs about 470 VGPRs (it uses no LDS at all). `waves_per_eu=2` caps the budget at 256, so the excess spills to scratch inside the KV loop.

**An LLVM scheduler regression in Triton >= 3.7.** The same config that fit on 3.6 does not on 3.7+, which is what turned this from latent to visible. TTIR and TTGIR are byte-identical across the three versions and the LLVM IR instruction mix is the same; only the scratch size differs, so it is the AMDGPU machine scheduler producing longer live ranges, not anything in Triton's own passes.

**Config shadowing.** Because the lookup gives the leftmost axis priority, `D_GEQ_256` outranks `Q_GEQ_256`, so head sizes 256+ in prefill were picking a `BLOCK_M=16` entry meant for decode. That is why `d=256` was slower than `d=192` despite doing less work per program.

The goal is to fix all three without changing the default behavior so when a fix eventually lands in Triton, this change does not end up regressing the performance. The tuned configs trade occupancy for registers against one measured shape family, so they are exposed as an opt-in rather than made the default.

## Technical Details

Two files change: the gfx950 `DEFAULT.json` and `unified_attention_utils.py`.

**An opt-in config section.** A new `attn_2d.OPT_IN` section holds the retuned prefill entries and is merged into the lookup only when `AITER_TRITON_UA_FAST_PATH=1`. With the variable unset nothing changes: the section is never consulted, and all five pre-existing sections of `DEFAULT.json` are byte-identical to before. The core fix in these entries is `waves_per_eu=1`, which lifts the VGPR budget from 256 to 512 and eliminates the spill. It is scoped to head sizes 129+ (`D_GEQ_129` / `D_GEQ_256` keys) because sizes below that never spilled, and halving their occupancy target only costs them speed.

**The AMD backend workaround.** On top of the register fix, the opt-in entries can pass `amdgpu-sched-strategy=iterative-minreg` through Triton's `llvm_fn_attrs` option. This overrides the AMDGPU machine scheduler with a register-minimising strategy, recovering a further ~25% on large caches. It is not unconditionally good, so it sits in a `LARGE_KV` sub-block behind three guards:

- **Cache size.** Under `2**31` elements the backend indexes the cache with 32-bit buffer ops instead of 64-bit global loads. Against that different code the attribute costs about 3x rather than saving 25%. The guard counts elements, so if what the backend really tests is bytes, a borderline cache is declined rather than wrongly taken.
- **Dtype.** The overrides pay off for fp8 and cost bf16 about sixfold, so only the `DT_fp8_fp8` keys carry them.
- **Triton support.** `llvm_fn_attrs` is read off the backend's own options rather than inferred from a version number, and the block is skipped with a warning where the option does not exist.

## Test Plan

A standalone harness replays the Qwen3.5-397B debug shape and swaps configs through the lookup:

- **Coverage sweep** across head sizes 64-512, both prefill and decode, small (128-block) and large (4795-block) KV caches, fp8 and bf16, with the flag both unset and set. Each run reports the matched config entry, p50 latency, and the compiled kernel's scratch (register spill) bytes.
- **Guard tests** that exercise each of the three `LARGE_KV` gates: large cache with the option supported (applies), small cache (size guard declines), and a backend without `llvm_fn_attrs` (support guard declines). Also asserts the `LARGE_KV` sub-block never leaks into the launched config.
- **Numerics check** comparing the opt-in base and the large-KV overrides for bitwise-identical output, since the overrides only move scheduling and occupancy.
- **Regression guard on the default** by diffing every pre-existing section of `DEFAULT.json` against `HEAD` to confirm the flag-off path is untouched.

## Test Result

All pre-existing `DEFAULT.json` sections are byte-identical to `HEAD`; the only addition is `attn_2d.OPT_IN`. The guard tests pass (overrides apply only on a large fp8 cache with a supporting Triton, and never leak), and the opt-in base and large-KV overrides are bitwise identical.

gfx950, fp8, prefill. Small cache is 128 blocks, large is 4795. Each cell is p50 latency in ms (±0.1-0.2 ms run to run), with kernel scratch (register spill) in bytes in parentheses; "unchanged" means the opt-in section holds no entry for that head size, so the flag has no effect.

| head size | off, small cache (ms) | off, large cache (ms) | on, small cache (ms) | on, large cache (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64, 128 | 2.5-2.9 | 2.5-3.1 | unchanged | unchanged |
| 160, 192, 224 | 5.2-5.3 (132 B) | 12.1-12.2 (288 B) | 5.3 (0 B) | 4.6 (20 B) |
| 256 | 10.0 | 12.5 | 5.2 (0 B) | 4.7 (20 B) |
| 512 | 24.8 | 28.9 | unchanged | unchanged |

bf16, same shape, large cache is 2400 blocks. bf16 stays on the opt-in base config, since the large-KV overrides do not apply to it:

| head size | off, small cache (ms) | off, large cache (ms) | on, small cache (ms) | on, large cache (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 11.7 (236 B) | 31.1 (920 B) | 7.1 (0 B) | 8.7 (0 B) |
| 256 | 25.0 | 34.8 | 7.2 (0 B) | 8.7 (0 B) |

Spill drops from up to 920 B to at most 20 B on every affected head size (0 B except on the fp8 large cache, where the minreg override leaves 20 B). The `d=256` bf16 row is the shadowing fix on its own; the `d=192` row is the register fix, worth 3.6x on the large cache. Decode is untouched under both settings, as are head sizes 64, 128 and 512.

## Notes and follow-ups

- The opt-in section has four entries where two would do. `D_GEQ_256` shadows `D_GEQ_129.Q_GEQ_256`, so the config has to be repeated at each `D` bound, and again split by dtype because only fp8 takes the `LARGE_KV` block.
- These configs were tuned against one shape family. `waves_per_eu=1` trades occupancy for registers, which is why this is opt-in rather than the default.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] [GFX950] Unified Attention configs tuning
[Triton/Gluon] [Kernel] Add packed FP4 logical transpose
body:
## Summary

- Add `transpose_packed_fp4` for bit-exact logical transpose of row-major FP4 data packed as two nibbles per byte.
- Keep the kernel, wrapper, tests, and benchmark in the existing `fast_transpose` files.
- Support arbitrary input strides, non-power-of-two tails, `torch.uint8`, and `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2`.
- Reuse the existing 32 x 32 logical transpose tile and provide a kernel `repr` containing both tile parameters.

This is not a duplicate of `shuffle_weight_f4` or `shuffle_mxfp8fp4_b`: those operations rearrange 16 x 16 packed-byte tiles for GEMM layouts, while this operation produces the logical shape `(N, M / 2)` and repacks nibble pairs after transposition.

Closes #5537.

## Validation

Correctness on MI350X / gfx950 with ROCm 7.2:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q \
  op_tests/triton_tests/quant/test_fast_transpose.py
```

Result: `48 passed`.

The packed-FP4 cases cover nibble order, non-power-of-two tails, strided input, 64-bit stride arguments, native packed dtype preservation, validation, and round trips.

Static checks:

```bash
black --check --fast \
  aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/quant/fast_transpose.py \
  aiter/ops/triton/quant/__init__.py \
  aiter/ops/triton/quant/fast_transpose.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/quant/test_fast_transpose.py \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fast_transpose.py
ruff check \
  aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/quant/fast_transpose.py \
  aiter/ops/triton/quant/__init__.py \
  aiter/ops/triton/quant/fast_transpose.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/quant/test_fast_transpose.py \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fast_transpose.py
python -m compileall -q \
  aiter/ops/triton/_triton_kernels/quant/fast_transpose.py \
  aiter/ops/triton/quant/__init__.py \
  aiter/ops/triton/quant/fast_transpose.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/quant/test_fast_transpose.py \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fast_transpose.py
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

Result: Black, Ruff, compileall, and `git diff --check` passed.

Benchmark reproducer:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. \
  python op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_fast_transpose.py \
  --op packed_fp4 --metric time
```

| Logical shape | PyTorch (ms) | AITER (ms) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 6144 x 4096 | 0.349391 | 0.064508 | 5.42x |
| 4096 x 4096 | 0.324700 | 0.057674 | 5.63x |
| 24576 x 4096 | 0.938870 | 0.103893 | 9.04x |
| 4096 x 12288 | 0.600084 | 0.094868 | 6.33x |

The benchmark uses 25 warmup iterations and 100 timed repetitions. A maintainer needs to add `ci:triton-300x` for gfx942 coverage; fork authors cannot add repository labels.

## Checklist

- [x] Kernel has `repr`.
- [x] Unit tests are included.
- [x] Benchmark is included.
- [x] Files follow the existing quant/fast-transpose layout.
- [x] Existing transpose and FP4 shuffle implementations were checked for duplicate functionality.
- [x] No new common helper or third-party dependency.
- [x] No breaking API change.
- [x] Signed off under the project contribution policy.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Kernel] Add fused SiLU-and-multiply backward
body:
## Summary

Add a fused Triton backward operation for `silu(gate) * up` with concatenated
`[gate, up]` input layout.

Closes #5541.

## Motivation

AITER already provides the SiLU-and-multiply forward operation, but training
currently builds its backward from multiple eager PyTorch operations. This PR
adds the matching fused backward while keeping the implementation in the
existing activation family.

## Changes

- Add `_silu_and_mul_backward_kernel` beside the existing SiLU-and-multiply
  forward kernel and reuse the shared `_sigmoid_exp2` device helper.
- Add `silu_and_mul_backward(grad_output, x, out=None)` to
  `aiter.ops.triton.activation`.
- Evaluate SiLU and both gradient products in FP32 before converting to the
  input dtype.
- Support FP16, BF16, and FP32, arbitrary leading dimensions, strided
  `grad_output`, optional preallocated output, empty rows, and non-current-GPU
  launches.
- Add a config-aware kernel `repr`, unit tests, a benchmark, and the measured
  gfx950 tuning configuration.
- Reuse a shared `select_leq_config` helper for upper-bound config tables and
  migrate the two existing local copies in `fused_clamp_act_mul` and
  `fused_add_rmsnorm_pad`.
- Route the touched config reads through `resolve_config_dir()` and document
  the shared selector in the config rulebooks.
- Correct the shared VGPR table parser for benchmark labels containing units.

## Hardware support and tuning

This PR supports **gfx950 only**. It does not ship or claim support for gfx942;
an unsupported architecture fails required-config resolution with the missing
architecture-specific path.

The measured config is stored at:

```text
aiter/ops/triton/configs/gfx950/triton/fusions/silu_and_mul_backward/DEFAULT.json
```

`width` below is the gate/up width, so `x.shape[-1] == 2 * width`.
`select_leq_config` chooses the smallest matching `N_LEQ_*` entry and otherwise
uses `any`:

| Width | `BLOCK_M` | `BLOCK_N` | `num_warps` | `num_stages` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `<= 64` | 32 | 64 | 4 | 1 |
| `<= 128` | 32 | 128 | 4 | 1 |
| `<= 256` | 16 | 256 | 4 | 1 |
| `<= 512` | 8 | 512 | 4 | 1 |
| `> 512` | 4 | 1024 | 4 | 1 |

`BLOCK_M` and `BLOCK_N` are the row and column tiles. At launch, `BLOCK_M` is
capped by the next power of two of the row count; widths above 1024 use
multiple column tiles. `num_warps` and `num_stages` control launch scheduling.
The kernel `repr` records the effective `BLOCK_M` and `BLOCK_N` specialization.

## Performance

Measured at commit `74dcacab94842bac67e59b50e202ecea2b129672`.

- GPU: AMD Instinct MI350X VF (`gfx950`)
- ROCm: 7.2.4
- HIP runtime: 7.2.53211
- Python: 3.10.12
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+rocm7.2`
- Triton: 3.7.0
- dtype: BF16
- Timing: `triton.testing.do_bench`, `warmup=25 ms`, `rep=100 ms`, arithmetic mean

Commands:

```bash
for width in 4096 12288; do
  for metric in time bandwidth; do
    ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=. \
      python op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_silu_and_mul_backward.py \
      --width "${width}" --dtype bf16 --provider all --metric "${metric}" \
      --warmup 25 --rep 100
  done
done
```

Each provider is measured by an independent `do_bench` invocation. `aiter`
measures the allocation-inclusive public API (`out=None`),
`aiter-preallocated` allocates `out` before timing, and `torch` is an
FP32-intermediate eager implementation of the same derivative. There was no
previous AITER backward operator, so the eager implementation is the functional
baseline rather than a before/after AITER kernel baseline.

### Latency and speedup

| Rows | Width | Preallocated `out` (us) | `out=None` (us) | FP32 eager (us) | Speedup: preallocated / `out=None` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4,096 | 10.095 | 7.806 | 89.599 | 8.88x / 11.48x |
| 128 | 4,096 | 6.817 | 6.939 | 87.115 | 12.78x / 12.55x |
| 2,048 | 4,096 | 32.894 | 33.041 | 234.537 | 7.13x / 7.10x |
| 8,192 | 4,096 | 107.258 | 107.228 | 1,032.173 | 9.62x / 9.63x |
| 1 | 12,288 | 11.821 | 10.054 | 104.233 | 8.82x / 10.37x |
| 128 | 12,288 | 9.110 | 11.659 | 104.813 | 11.50x / 8.99x |
| 2,048 | 12,288 | 89.151 | 89.169 | 757.152 | 8.49x / 8.49x |
| 8,192 | 12,288 | 256.765 | 256.638 | 3,079.848 | 11.99x / 12.00x |

Geometric-mean speedup over the FP32 eager reference is **9.73x** with a
preallocated output and **9.92x** through the allocation-inclusive public API.
For rows >= 2048, the two AITER paths differ by at most 0.45%; sub-percent
differences are measurement noise, not evidence that allocation improves the
kernel. Small cases are launch/API-latency bound.

### Effective bandwidth

Logical BF16 traffic is three input reads plus two output writes per gate/up
pair:

```text
5 * rows * width * sizeof(bfloat16) = 10 * rows * width bytes
```

Utilization uses AMD's published MI350X peak theoretical HBM bandwidth of
[8.0 TB/s per GPU](https://www.amd.com/en/products/accelerators/instinct/mi350/mi350x.html),
or 8,000 GB/s in decimal units.

| Rows | Width | Logical bytes | Preallocated GB/s (% peak) | `out=None` GB/s (% peak) | FP32 eager logical GB/s (% peak) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4,096 | 40,960 | 4.1 (0.05%) | 5.2 (0.07%) | 0.5 (0.01%) |
| 128 | 4,096 | 5,242,880 | 769.1 (9.61%) | 755.5 (9.44%) | 60.2 (0.75%) |
| 2,048 | 4,096 | 83,886,080 | 2,550.2 (31.88%) | 2,538.9 (31.74%) | 357.7 (4.47%) |
| 8,192 | 4,096 | 335,544,320 | 3,128.4 (39.10%) | 3,129.3 (39.12%) | 325.1 (4.06%) |
| 1 | 12,288 | 122,880 | 10.4 (0.13%) | 12.2 (0.15%) | 1.2 (0.01%) |
| 128 | 12,288 | 15,728,640 | 1,726.5 (21.58%) | 1,349.1 (16.86%) | 150.1 (1.88%) |
| 2,048 | 12,288 | 251,658,240 | 2,822.8 (35.29%) | 2,822.3 (35.28%) | 332.4 (4.15%) |
| 8,192 | 12,288 | 1,006,632,960 | 3,920.4 (49.01%) | 3,922.4 (49.03%) | 326.8 (4.09%) |

The eager path uses the same logical-byte denominator for comparison, but it
performs additional physical traffic for FP32 casts, intermediates, separate
pointwise kernels, concatenation, and the final BF16 cast. Its reported value
is useful/logical bandwidth, not measured HBM traffic. The local GPU is exposed
as a virtual function, and the 8.0 TB/s figure is an advertised theoretical
full-GPU peak rather than sustained application bandwidth.

### Roofline estimate

Per gate/up pair, the fused kernel transfers 10 logical bytes and performs
approximately 11 ordinary FP32 operations plus one `exp2`, or about
**1.1 FLOP/byte** when the transcendental is excluded from the FLOP count.
AMD publishes 144.2 TFLOP/s peak FP32 vector performance and 8.0 TB/s peak HBM
bandwidth for MI350X, giving an estimated roofline ridge point of
`144.2 / 8.0 = 18.0 FLOP/byte`.

Because 1.1 FLOP/byte is far below 18.0 FLOP/byte, the conventional roofline
predicts a bandwidth-bound kernel at sufficiently large shapes. The largest
cases reach about 39-49% of advertised peak HBM bandwidth. This is an estimate:
`exp2` throughput, non-payload traffic, virtualization, and QoS are not modeled.

## Validation

MI350X/gfx950 targeted correctness, including width 1, strided gradients,
explicit output, empty rows, unsupported gfx942 config behavior, and a
non-current-GPU launch:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q \
  op_tests/triton_tests/fusions/test_silu_and_mul_backward.py
```

Result: `53 passed`.

Kernel and config-loader regression suite:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q \
  op_tests/triton_tests/fusions/test_silu_and_mul_backward.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/fusions/test_fused_clamp_act_mul.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/normalization/test_fused_add_rmsnorm_pad.py
```

Result: `1223 passed, 874 skipped`.

Activation-family regression suite:

```bash
GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q \
  op_tests/triton_tests/test_activation.py \
  op_tests/triton_tests/fusions/test_fused_silu_mul.py
```

Result: `419 passed, 228 skipped`.

Width-one benchmark smoke test:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_silu_and_mul_backward.py \
  --rows 3 --width 1 --provider all --metric time --warmup 5 --rep 20
```

Result: all providers completed.

VGPR path:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. python \
  op_tests/op_benchmarks/triton/bench_silu_and_mul_backward.py \
  --rows 1 --width 64 --provider aiter --metric time \
  --warmup 1 --rep 1 --print-vgpr
```

Result: `_silu_and_mul_backward_kernel_BLOCK_M_1_BLOCK_N_64`, 11 VGPR, no
VGPR spill.

Ruff 0.16.0, Black 26.5.1, `compileall`, JSON parsing, and
`git diff --check` pass for all changed files.

## Documentation, dependencies, and compatibility

- The public wrapper documents the config parameters and gfx950-only support.
- The shared config selector is documented in `configs/CLAUDE.md`, the Triton
  maintainer guide, and the scoped review instructions.
- No new third-party dependency.
- No breaking change to an existing public API.
- The forward path remains the existing `aiter.silu_and_mul` operation.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add FP8 Flash Attention v2 kernel (gfx942/gfx950)
body:
## Summary

  Adds a pure-Triton FP8 Flash Attention v2 implementation supporting gfx942 and gfx950, including forward and backward passes with per-block FP8 scale tensors.

  The kernel selects architecture-specific FP8 dtypes at import time: gfx942 uses `float8e4b8`/`float8e5b16`, gfx950 uses `float8e4nv`/`float8e5`.

  ## Changes

  - `_triton_kernels/attention/fp8_attention_kernel.py`: Triton kernels for forward (`attn_fwd`) and backward (`_bwd_kernel_dkdv`, `_bwd_kernel_dq`,  `_bwd_preprocess_use_o`, `_attn_bwd_dkdv`, `_attn_bwd_dq`, `compute_fp8_scaling_factors`). All 7 public kernels have repr decorators. Autotune configs resolved via `get_tuned_kernel_config()` backed by per-arch JSON, removing hardcoded Python tile values. Removes duplicate `is_cdna4()` definition in favour of import from `arch_info`.
  - `utils/_triton/arch_info.py`: Add `is_cdna4()` canonical definition.
  - `configs/gfx942/triton/attention/fp8_attn/DEFAULT.json` +`configs/gfx950/triton/attention/fp8_attn/DEFAULT.json`: Pinned tile configs for forward and backward kernels.
  - `triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_attention_kernel.py`: Correctness tests for `attn_fwd` (USE_FP8=False) against PyTorch reference.
  - `bench_fp8_attention.py`: Benchmark with `--causal` and `-metric` options.

  ## Test results

  Verified on **MI350X (gfx950)** and **MI308X (gfx942)**:

  pytest -v op_tests/triton_tests/attention/test_fp8_attention_kernel.py
  10 passed, 2 skipped in ~10s

  ✅ MHA / GQA (num_q_heads ≠ num_kv_heads)
  ✅ causal on / off
  ✅ bf16 / fp16
  ✅ S_q ≠ S_k (non-causal)
  ⏭ causal + S_q ≠ S_k (intentionally skipped — undefined behavior)

  Note: Tests cover the USE_FP8=False (BF16/FP16) forward path. The USE_FP8=True path is not yet tested.

title: [Triton/Gluon] Add MXFP8 Flash Attention v2 (gfx950 / CDNA4)
body:
## Summary

  Adds a pure-Triton MXFP8 Flash Attention v2 implementation for gfx950 (CDNA4 / MI300X), including forward and backward passes.

  Uses MXFP8 block-scaling (E8M0 microscales, one uint8 per 32 elements along the head dimension). Requires gfx950; asserts at runtime on other architectures.

  ## Changes

  - `_triton_kernels/attention/mxfp8_attention_kernel.py`: Triton kernels for forward (`attn_fwd_mxfp8`) and backward (`_bwd_kernel_dkdv_mxfp8`, `_bwd_kernel_dq_mxfp8`, `_bwd_preprocess_use_o_mxfp8`). All 6 public kernels have repr decorators. Autotune configs resolved via `get_tuned_kernel_config()` backed by JSON. Dead code removed (`get_padded_headsize`, `get_input_shapes`).
  - `attention/mxfp8_attention.py`: Python wrappers `mxfp8_attention_forward` and `mxfp8_attention_backward`.
  - `utils/_triton/arch_info.py`: Add canonical `is_cdna4()` definition (was used in `__init__.py` and the wrapper but missing from the module).
  - `configs/gfx950/triton/attention/mxfp8_attn/DEFAULT.json`: Per-arch pinned tile config.
  - `__init__.py`: Export `mxfp8_attention` under the `_CDNA4_ONLY` gate.
  - `triton_tests/attention/test_mxfp8_attention_kernel.py`: Correctness  tests (skip on non-gfx950 architectures).
  - `bench_mxfp8_attention.py`: Benchmark across representative shapes.

  ## Test results

  Verified on **MI350X (gfx950)**:
  ✅ MHA / GQA (num_q_heads ≠ num_kv_heads)
  ✅ causal on / off
  ✅ bf16 and fp16 (use_mxfp8=False: verifies core attention correctness without MXFP8 quantization)

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] Enable unified-attention skip-mask for gfx950 hd256 FP8 prefill
body:
## Summary

- Enable the existing `SPLIT_UNMASKED_LOOP` fast path for gfx950 head-size-256 FP8 Q / FP8 KV, non-windowed, non-shuffled prefill with `max_seqlen_q >= 256`.
- This is config-only: the kernel and wrapper from [AITER PR #4761](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4761) are unchanged.
- Add the head-size-256 `Q_GEQ_256` config family while keeping sliding-window and shuffled variants on the non-skip path.
- Restore efficient long-context FP8-Q unified prefill: the exact [SGLang PR #39998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39998) parent stack regresses badly at long context without this config, while [AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) recovers and exceeds the true-stock serving baseline.

## Why

[AITER PR #4761](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4761) enabled skip-mask only for `D_LEQ_128.Q_GEQ_256.DT_fp8_fp8`. Qwen3.8-27B full-attention layers use `head_dim=256`, so they match `D_GEQ_256` first and never reach the head-size-128 key.

This PR adds `D_GEQ_256.Q_GEQ_256.DT_fp8_fp8` with `BLOCK_M=128`, tile 64, and `SPLIT_UNMASKED_LOOP=true`. Sliding-window and shuffled siblings use the same long-prefill tile without enabling the skip loop. Lookup continues to prefer `D_GEQ_512` for head size 512, while decode continues to prefer `D_GEQ_256.Q_LEQ_1*`.

## Activation requirements

This config is used only when SGLang routes prefill through AITER unified attention:

- `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`
- `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`
- `attention-backend=aiter`
- FP8 Q conversion from [SGLang PR #39998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39998)

For full AITER page-size-1 decode, the CUDA-graph page-table fix from [SGLang PR #40410](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40410) is also required. The stock/parent/candidate crossover below used Triton decode for every arm, avoiding the affected unified-decode path while preserving the AITER prefill comparison.

## Controlled stock, parent, and candidate comparison

The primary comparison used the same MI355X host, TP1, Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 model, FP8 KV, seeds, prompt counts, request shapes, and Triton compiler in every arm.

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| Triton | `3.8.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git7cb7b059` |
| Triton wheel SHA256 | `2aa39a413aab73901e1e4b3a166495a17d2325ac9cedf0e8c77a1f0df661b71a` |
| Chunked prefill | 16384 |
| Decode backend | Triton for all arms |
| True stock | [SGLang PR #39598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39598), legacy `mha_batch_prefill_*` |
| Parent | SGLang [PR #39998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39998), parent AITER unified Triton config |
| Candidate | Same parent stack plus [AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) |
| Stock image | `sha256:6457bcaf548be73cebfd9ca6650e43ecb8ba78d82ce87e1f4b33696075bc7e5e` |
| Parent image | `sha256:0223e66ecfb6c5773cb22ff495dd213f5aaf4c79c897ace8ba9697ce7345bd5d` |
| Candidate image | `sha256:69aa235ad0bdf09674c6bb6bafa0fafc7a4bb36c819e7cf73a3dc062f1aaec9d` |

Each arm ran on HIP 4 and HIP 6 in a crossover schedule. All 48 child benchmark runs completed. Cross-GPU output-throughput variance was below 3% except the candidate 128K/c16 row at 3.83%, which remains explicitly flagged.

Route probes confirmed:

- True stock used legacy `mha_batch_prefill_*`.
- Parent used FP8-Q/FP8-KV unified Triton fallback.
- Candidate selected unified Triton with `BLOCK_M=128` and `SPLIT_UNMASKED_LOOP=true`.
- Every arm used Triton decode.

Short-answer, 60K needle, and sampled GPQA smoke gates passed in every arm.

## Direct unified-attention kernel evidence

The kernel gate uses the production Qwen3.8 geometry: 24 Q heads, 4 KV heads, head dimension 256, page size 1, and FP8 Q / FP8 KV. Both parent and candidate completed 18/18 executable cases with zero runtime errors and zero quantized-reference failures.

Measured after one warmup invocation:

| Prefill shape | Parent config | [#5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) config | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q=16K, KV=16K | 9.16 ms | 2.94 ms | 3.12× |
| Q=16K, KV=64K | 88.18 ms | 15.37 ms | 5.74× |
| Q=16K, KV=128K | 218.02 ms | 32.92 ms | 6.62× |

The short-Q and decode probes remained close, which matches the PR scope: the new key targets long prefill rather than decode.

At Q=16K and KV=16K, the candidate FP8-Q output had approximately 0.9998 cosine similarity to the quantized-input reference and passed the configured tolerance. The same output had approximately 0.9988 cosine similarity and 91.6% head-output argmax agreement versus the original BF16 reference.

## End-to-end serving evidence

Output throughput is the median of the HIP 4 and HIP 6 crossover runs.

| Workload | True stock | [#39998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39998) parent | [#5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) candidate | Candidate vs stock | Candidate vs parent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K/1K c4 | 303.68 | 300.41 | 298.84 | −1.6% | −0.5% |
| 8K/1K c16 | 844.34 | 835.33 | 850.12 | +0.7% | +1.8% |
| 60K/600 c4 | 129.93 | 97.75 | 142.43 | +9.6% | +45.7% |
| 60K/600 c16 | 179.65 | 123.75 | 203.50 | +13.3% | +64.5% |
| 128K/1K c4 | 84.25 | 53.98 | 99.67 | +18.3% | +84.6% |
| 128K/1K c16 | 102.21 | 60.41 | 125.10 | +22.4% | +107.1% |

Variance-adjusted output-throughput geometric-mean deltas:

- [SGLang PR #39998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39998) parent versus true stock: −24.04%.
- [AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) candidate versus true stock: +10.10%.
- [AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) candidate versus its exact parent: +44.95%.

The context trend is the important result. The candidate is approximately flat at 8K and improves progressively at 60K and 128K. This is consistent with the direct kernel measurements and demonstrates why the head-size-256 long-prefill config is needed.

## Corrected full-stack validation

A separate corrected page-size-1 stack added [SGLang PR #40410](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40410) and kept Triton `7cb7b059`. Full correctness validation produced:

- GPQA: 48.48% over 198 samples, matching the BF16-Q parent.
- NIAH: 100% at both 64K and 128K over 1,000 total samples.
- MMMU: 59.11% over 900 samples, within the planned two-point tolerance.

The corrected TP1+TP2 40-row text and multimodal sweep completed every expected request. Absolute output-throughput geomeans were:

- Text: 603.49 tok/s.
- Multimodal: 427.99 tok/s.
- Overall: 525.98 tok/s.

These absolute numbers are not a stock-versus-candidate isolation; the crossover table above is the direct PR comparison.

## Complementary Gluon result

On the same corrected Triton `7cb7b059` stack, [AITER PR #4614](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4614) at `f54d368` plus runtime-stride [commit `89f96298`](https://github.com/vorapolsiloai/aiter/commit/89f9629872726be8c93fcc896d53577c83705dbc) measured 622.82 tok/s on text, 415.83 tok/s on multimodal, and 529.89 tok/s overall.

The implementations are complementary: adjusted Gluon is stronger on text, while [AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) remains stronger on important multimodal shapes. Because this PR changes only the Triton config, it remains useful as the fallback even if the Gluon implementation merges.

## Triton compiler sensitivity

An older [AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) image used `triton==3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.0.0` and did not contain [SGLang PR #40410](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40410). Its overall 40-row output-throughput geomean was 540.15 tok/s versus 525.98 tok/s for the corrected Triton `7cb7b059` stack, a −2.6% stack-level difference.

This is not a clean compiler-only A/B because [SGLang PR #40410](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40410) also changed. A `4cff872c` run with the page-table fix is needed to isolate the compiler contribution. The older result is not a correctness-valid deployment result because it lacks the page-size-1 fix.

## Interpretation

[AITER PR #5598](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5598) fixes a severe long-context configuration gap in the FP8-Q parent path:

- 3.12–6.62× faster direct long-prefill kernels.
- +44.95% end-to-end output-throughput geomean versus its exact [SGLang PR #39998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39998) parent.
- +10.10% end-to-end output-throughput geomean versus true stock.
- Near-neutral behavior at 8K.

It is a low-risk, config-only improvement and remains valuable as the Triton implementation and fallback independently of the Gluon work.

## Test plan

- [x] Validate exact route selection for true stock, parent, and candidate.
- [x] Validate the current `BLOCK_M=128`, tile-64, skip-enabled config.
- [x] Run direct kernel correctness and timing gates on Qwen3.8 production geometry.
- [x] Run the six-row stock/parent/candidate crossover on HIP 4 and HIP 6.
- [x] Verify all 48 child serving runs complete.
- [x] Run short-answer, 60K needle, and sampled GPQA smoke gates in every crossover arm.
- [x] Run corrected full GPQA, NIAH-64K/128K, and MMMU gates.
- [x] Run corrected TP1 and TP2 40-row text and multimodal sweeps.
- [ ] Run the complete AITER unified-attention test matrix on gfx950.

title: [Triton/Gluon] fix(gluon): two-step addressing in paged MQA logits kernel (pool coord -> block column + offset)
body:
## Summary

The gluon port of `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (`aiter/ops/triton/gluon/pa_mqa_logits.py`) indexes the `kv_indices` block table with the **raw pool coordinate** instead of converting it to a block-table column first. This overruns the table row by up to `KVBlockSize`× (64× on gfx942), reads a garbage physical block id, and then dereferences `KV_buffer[garbage * stride_k_seq]` → **arbitrary-address read → deterministic Memory access fault on all TP ranks**.

The Triton reference implementation (`ops/triton/_triton_kernels/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py`) already does this correctly:

```python
logical_block_idx = logical_kv_idx // KVBlockSize   # block-table column
block_offset      = logical_kv_idx % KVBlockSize    # offset within block
```

This PR ports the same **two-step addressing** to the gluon kernel at all three load sites (prologue prefetch / in-loop prefetch / `k_next` + scale consumption), and hardens the prefetch masks to bound **both** directions (`>= 0 && < context_length`) with out-of-window lanes forced to 0, so a garbage block id can never reach the `KV_buffer` dereference.

## Root cause detail

`kv_indices` rows are **BLOCK tables**: column `j` holds the physical block id for pools `[j*KVBlockSize, (j+1)*KVBlockSize)`. `context_length` is a **pool count** that can reach `max_block_len × KVBlockSize`. The buggy code used the pool coordinate directly as the column index:

```python
# before (bug): pool coord used as block-table column
context_kv_idx_next = buffer_load(
    kv_indices,
    offsets=pid_batch * max_block_len + context_idx + arange)  # overruns row 64x
k_next = buffer_load(KV_buffer, offsets=context_kv_idx_next * stride_k_seq + arange)
```

```python
# after (fix): two-step addressing, matches Triton reference semantics
block_col = pool_pos // KVBlockSize
block_off = pool_pos % KVBlockSize
context_kv_idx = buffer_load(kv_indices, offsets=pid_batch * max_block_len + block_col, mask=...)
k_next = buffer_load(KV_buffer, offsets=context_kv_idx * stride_k_seq + block_off * HiddenDim + ...)
```

## Reproduction (before fix)

- **Hardware**: 8× MI308X (gfx942), TP4, ROCm 7.2, triton 3.7
- **Model**: GLM-5.3-Flash (fp8 e4m3 KV cache, page 64, `index_kpool=4`, kpool indexer → `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` with `Preshuffle=False`)
- **Trigger**: any request whose KV length exceeds **16384 tokens** (= 4096 pools × 4) faults deterministically on the **first decode step** after prefill completes; 8K passes. 4 ranks fault simultaneously (KFD, `Reason: Unknown`).
- **Forensics**: `AMD_LOG_LEVEL=3` + `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `--disable-cuda-graph` pins the faulting kernel to `_gluon_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (last synchronous launch before the fault).
- **Version-independence**: reproduced identically on aiter 7/29, 8/29, and 9/15-main (full Python/Triton/C++ rebuild) — the bug is in the gluon port itself.
- **No env switch**: `enable_gluon_pa_mqa_logits` auto-enables on gfx942/gfx950/gfx1250 with triton ≥ 3.5, so any GLM-5.x / DSV4-class kpool-indexer workload with > 16K context hits this on stock ROCm 7.2 containers.

## Verification (after fix)

| Seq length | tokens | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 7,460 | PASS | PASS 1.4s (no regression) |
| 20K | 20,166 | **100% crash** (4-rank fault) | **PASS 3.3s** |
| 32K | 32,720 | always crash | PASS 6.9s |
| 64K | 65,697 | always crash | PASS 12.6s |
| 128K | 133,136 | always crash | PASS 32.4s |

- 20K regression ×2: stable PASS.
- CUDA graph output matches eager **token-for-token** (rules out stale pool-table in capture).
- Zero `Memory access fault` across the full sweep.

## Notes for reviewers

- The fix keeps the gluon layout idioms (SliceLayout arange, `buffer_load`, `_amd_iglp_sched_barrier`) — only the addressing arithmetic and mask bounds change.
- An alternative sglang-side workaround (switching to the `_preshuffle` variant via `Preshuffle=True`) also works but requires a pre-shuffled KV layout; this PR fixes the non-preshuffle path at the source.
- Happy to add a unit test if maintainers point me at the preferred test harness for gluon kernels (I did not find an existing `pa_mqa_logits` gluon test to extend).

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Config] gfx1151 gemma4 attn prefill tuning
body:
Tuning for large head_size=512 attn_2d tuning for Strix Halo, of fp8/bf16 KV cache.

## Motivation
vLLM's default `TRITON_ATTN` backend doesn't offer optimal tuning config for gfx1151, and there isn't per-arch tunning opportunity.

## Test Result

### Kernel-level, bf16 KV / bf16 Q

| kv_len | q_len | block | TRITON_ATTN (ms) | AITER before (ms) | AITER tuned (ms) | tuned vs before (improvement) | tuned vs TRITON_ATTN (improvement) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 32,768 | 16 | 12830.31 | 4215.41 | 2211.04 | 1.91× | 5.80× |
| 32,768 | 32,768 | 64 | 11119.52 | 4050.21 | 2265.70 | 1.79× | 4.91× |
| 32,768 | 2,048 | 16 | 1390.79 | 425.65 | 205.97 | 2.07× | 6.75× |
| 32,768 | 2,048 | 64 | 1296.01 | 432.48 | 200.48 | 2.16× | 6.46× |

### Kernel-level, fp8 KV / bf16 Q

| kv_len | TRITON_ATTN (ms) | AITER before (ms) | AITER tuned (ms) | tuned vs before (improvement) | tuned vs TRITON_ATTN (improvement) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32,768 | 1452.3 | 971.8 | 615.1 | 1.58× | 2.36× |
| 60,000 | 2723.7 | 1789.8 | 1193.2 | 1.50× | 2.28× |

### Model-level, `vllm bench serve`

32768-in / 32-out, `--max-num-seqs 1`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--num-prompts 4`

| backend | KV | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| TRITON_ATTN | bf16 | 146005.21 | 73.58 |
| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | bf16 | 20117.60 | 50.59 |
| TRITON_ATTN | fp8 | 164764.79 | 85.09 |
| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | fp8 | 63824.95 | 70.63 |

| comparison | Median TTFT improvement | Median TPOT improvement|
|---|---:|---:|
| tuned vs TRITON_ATTN, bf16 KV | 7.26× | 1.45× |
| tuned vs TRITON_ATTN, fp8 KV | 2.58× | 1.20× |

## Potential problem
Using TRITON=`3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.1.0a20260811`, the compiler has an **uneven** cost upcasting fp8 to bf16/fp16, and the following local patch is required in vLLM to always pass in bf16 Q into the kernel.
`vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_aiter_unified_attn.py`, in `RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionImpl.__init__`:

```python
from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx11
self.supports_quant_query_input = not on_gfx11()
```

Without it, `Attention.__init__` builds a `query_quant` whenever the KV cache is fp8 (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:464-470`) and the query is quantized alongside the KV cache to fp8. 

### REASON
As gfx1151 has no fp8 WMMA, passing in fp8 Q is not only a pure precision loss, but also causes the kernel to regress up to 4 times. The Triton compiler's current default WMMA upcasting dtype is fp16, not bf16. Fp16 uses a lot more cmp instructions and causes the kernel to regress badly. Leaving Q in bf16, then inside kernel do `K_load.to(Q.dtype)`, `V_load.to(Q.dtype)` explicitly uses bf16 and bypasses the compiler problem. This is what the above table measurements are based on.

For conclusion, this is a pure use case problem, and this PR stays valid. Investigation into Triton compiler's RDNA3 fp8 upcasting dtype (fp16/bf16) is ongoing.

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [Triton/Gluon] [Bugfix] [Perf] Fix non-preshuffle MQA paging and large KV offsets, retune the decode grid, and cut plain-path instruction count
body:
## Summary

Four defects in the paged MQA logits decode path, all silent: no fault, no NaN or Inf, just wrong or missing logits.

The branch has since picked up two pieces of performance work on the same path, both originally reviewed as stacked PRs and now folded in: the decode grid sizing from #5711 and its follow-up, and the two instruction-level changes to the plain kernel from #5700. They are described in their own sections below and neither touches the correctness of the four fixes.

**1. Block paging for non-preshuffled multi-token blocks.** With `Preshuffle=False` and `KVBlockSize > 1` the Gluon kernel used token positions as page-table columns and always read token 0's K values and scale from each physical block. Compact block tables caused illegal memory accesses; padding the table kept the reads in allocated memory but produced incorrect logits. Resolve the physical block with `token_pos // KVBlockSize` and add the in-block token offset to both the K and the scale address, in the initial loads and in the prefetch loop. This fixes the failures reproduced in #5591. Related: #5600.

**2. KV caches past 2 GiB in the plain kernel.** That kernel forms a per-token address from the page table, so `physical_block * stride` overflowed a 32-bit product and wrapped into another page once the cache crossed 2 GiB. Its KV and scale strides are now 64-bit for every shape and the loads go through global pointers. A size-dependent switch between a 32-bit and a 64-bit variant was considered and dropped: it gives one shape two ABIs behind one AOT directory name, and the measured cost of always using 64-bit is bounded (see Performance).

**3. KV caches past 2 GiB in the preshuffle kernel.** When `ChunkKPerStage % KVBlockSize != 0`, which is `KVBlockSize=256` at `ChunkK=256`, the K and scale addresses came from the same 32-bit page-index product. Read them through a global pointer with the index promoted to 64 bits, the way the other branch of that kernel already does.

**4. Preshuffle tail store reaching into the next output row.** The branch that loads a page index per lane stored its last stage across the whole tile, including the columns past `context_length` that hold `-inf`. When the output width equals an unaligned context those columns land in the next row: with `context_lengths=(3001, 513)` and a compact output, row 1 lost its first 7 logits. Those three stores are now bounded by `max_model_len`, which the kernel's six other stores already did.

## Changes

- Correct block-table, K and scale addressing for sectioned, non-preshuffled caches, and keep negative positions in the backward-shifted first tile mapped to token 0 of physical block 0 after masking the page-table load.
- Generate the new address arithmetic only for `KVBlockSize > 1`, preserving the original scalar-first expressions, code generation and register usage for `KVBlockSize=1`.
- Use 64-bit KV and scale strides in the plain kernel unconditionally, and drop the now dead 32-bit load paths.
- Promote the preshuffle per-stage K and scale addresses to 64 bits.
- Bound the preshuffle per-lane stores by `max_model_len`.
- Extend `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py`: 48 paging cases (block sizes 1/16/64/128, chunks 64/256, compact and padded tables, randomized physical pages, per-token scales, short and empty contexts, MTP, multiple prefetch iterations) and 12 large-offset cases (plain `B1`/`B64` and preshuffle `B64`/`B256`, each at the 2, 4 and 8 GiB boundaries) against an independent FP32 reference, plus the two existing output-offset cases.

Note for AOT users: the plain kernel's stride arguments changed from `i32` to `i64`, its instruction stream changed again with the two optimizations below, and the preshuffle kernel's instruction stream changed, so cached `.hsaco` artifacts have to be regenerated from this branch. The grid change does not add to that — `SplitKV` is a runtime `i32` argument, not a `constexpr`, so it is not part of the compile key.

## Decode grid sizing

`deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` derived `SplitKV` from the batch and rounded **SplitKV** up to a multiple of five, but the thing that has to line up with the CU count is the **grid**, and the two differ by a factor of `TileQCount`. At batch 16/32/64 on 256 CU that landed on 2.5 workgroups per CU, so half the CUs ran three and half ran two and the kernel waited for the deeper half. The grid is now sized directly at two workgroups per CU, clamped so splits that start past the end of the context are not launched.

Two per CU is not enough at the top of the batch range, where each workgroup ends up chewing 128 to 256 chunks with no queue behind it, so a second term raises `SplitKV` toward 32 chunks per workgroup — by at most 2x, because `max_model_len` is only an upper bound on the real context and a loose bound must not be able to over-split without limit.

Scoring each candidate rule by how far its pick sits from the best `SplitKV` measured at each of 42 shapes:

| rule | exact | 4x over-estimate | 16x | 64x |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| the original formula | 7.69% | 7.69% | 7.69% | 7.69% |
| two per CU (context-free) | 0.85% | 0.87% | 0.89% | 0.89% |
| + cap 32 chunks/WG, unbounded | 0.46% | 1.69% | 7.45% | 20.11% |
| **+ cap 32, at most 2x** | **0.56%** | **1.40%** | **2.87%** | **4.08%** |

Against the original formula, at `N=131072`:

| layout | batch | SplitKV | grid | before | after | change |
| --- | ---: | :---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| plain | 1 | 520→512 | 520→512 | 5.95 | 5.96 | +0.22% |
| plain | 16 | 40→32 | 640→512 | 60.32 | **51.59** | **−14.46%** |
| plain | 64 | 10→16 | 640→1024 | 274.44 | **233.42** | **−14.95%** |
| plain | 128 | 10→8 | 1280→1024 | 469.96 | **456.88** | −2.78% |
| plain | 256 | 10→4 | 2560→1024 | 913.21 | 926.29 | **+1.43%** |
| preshuffle | 16 | 40→32 | 640→512 | 49.54 | **42.65** | **−13.92%** |
| preshuffle | 64 | 10→16 | 640→1024 | 249.40 | **220.28** | **−11.68%** |
| preshuffle | 128 | 10→8 | 1280→1024 | 465.27 | **445.93** | −4.16% |

Over 48 shapes (batch 1..256, context 8k/32k/128k, `next_n` 1 and 2, both layouts) the median is −2.01%, 21 shapes improve by more than 5%, the best is −18.90%, and zero mismatches. Batch 256 at a 128k context is the one shape that stays slower: its grid was already an exact 10 per CU so it never paid the quantisation cost, and its curve is a broad plateau on which the old value sat near the middle. Closing the remaining 1.9% would need the real context length, which lives in a device tensor.

The optional `SplitKV` argument added here is an override in the same spirit as the existing `TotalCuCount`; it is what lets both arms of the measurements come from a single binary. `gfx1250` keeps its own formula, having had no part available to re-tune on.

Correctness for this part: 62 passed, plus a 91-case scan aimed at the split seams — awkward chunk counts, non-uniform context lengths including `(8192, 8191, 1, 256, 257, 255, 65536, 3)` and `(20000, 3001, 513, 131072)`, contexts of length 1 and 2, exact multiples of `ChunkK` and one less, and `KVBlockSize` 1/16/64/256 on both layouts — zero mismatches over the whole output, masked region included.

## Plain-path instruction-level optimizations

Two changes to the `Preshuffle=False` Gluon kernel. Both are unconditional; the shape gate on the first is a correctness condition, not a switch.

**1. Hoist the KV block index and in-block offset out of the loop.** The kernel recomputed `token // KVBlockSize` and `token % KVBlockSize` over a `ChunkK`-wide vector every iteration. `KVBlockSize` is a `constexpr` power of two, so that should be one shift and one AND per register, but it expanded to 64 instructions because `context_idx` is loop-variant and the compiler cannot fold through it. `context_idx` advances by `ChunkK` and the gate requires `ChunkK % KVBlockSize == 0`, so the modulo is loop-invariant and the quotient grows by a constant. The identity does not require `context_idx` to be `KVBlockSize`-aligned, and `KVBlockSize > ChunkK` leaves the quotient without a constant stride, so those shapes keep the general form.

**2. Mask the logits after the head reduce, not before.** The kernel wrote `-inf` into the whole `(ChunkQ, ChunkK)` accumulator before reducing over heads, one `v_cndmask` per accumulator register: 32 in the loop and 32 more in the epilogue. Masking the reduced logits needs four and is the same value, since summing `ChunkQ` copies of `-inf` is `-inf`. The preshuffle kernel already masks after its reduce at all four of its store sites. Removing the `-inf` write also unblocks packed FP32 in the epilogue.

| | in-loop integer address ops | `v_cndmask` | `v_mul_f32` | `v_pk_add_f32` | `v_pk_mul_f32` | `v_pk_fma_f32` | VGPR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| before | 168 | 98 | 132 | 35 | 0 | 0 | 186 |
| + 1 | **76** | 98 | 132 | 35 | 0 | 0 | 188 |
| + 2 | **76** | **42** | **68** | **18** | **16** | **16** | 190 |

Neither improves register pressure: all three allocate 192 VGPR, so occupancy stays at 2 waves/SIMD.

Measured on top of the grid change above. Three worktrees run back to back inside each round with the arm order rotated, eight rounds; the statistic is the median of the per-round paired ratio, since clocks are not locked here and only pairing cancels the drift. `Preshuffle=True` is untouched by both, so its paired ratio is the noise floor.

| Batch | change 1 | change 2 | both | control (noise floor) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | −0.58% | **−2.83%** | **−3.57%** | +0.09% |
| 64 | −0.40% | **−1.02%** | **−1.36%** | +0.01% |
| 128 | −0.12% | **−0.69%** | **−0.80%** | +0.06% |

Change 2 carries almost all of the gain. Change 1 only just clears the noise floor at batch 16 and sits inside it at batch 128; it is worth keeping because it costs nothing and the instruction count genuinely drops, not because it is a measurable speedup on its own. **Batch 1 does not resolve and no claim is made for it**: over 16 paired rounds plain moves −0.97% with an IQR of [−3.08%, +0.28%] while the unchanged control moves +0.61% with an IQR of [−0.75%, +9.18%].

Both sides of the `HoistKvAddr` gate were measured at the same production scale:

| KVBlockSize | ChunkK | gate | b=16 | b=128 |
| ---: | ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 256 | on | −2.88% | −0.66% |
| 64 | 256 | on | −3.57% | −0.80% |
| 128 | 256 | on | −3.95% | −0.89% |
| 256 | 256 | on | −5.02% | −1.38% |
| 128 | 64 | **off** | −2.21% | −1.38% |
| 256 | 128 | **off** | −0.58% | −0.35% |
| 1 | 256 | **off** | −2.96% | — |

No shape regresses. The gated-off shapes still gain because change 2 is unconditional. `KVBlockSize=1` takes the branch where the logical index is never computed and `KVBlockSize > ChunkK` takes the branch where it is computed but the hoist is off, so all three paths are exercised; `op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py` already parametrises `block_size ∈ {1, 16, 64, 128} × chunk_k ∈ {64, 256}`, which covers the same split for correctness.

Change 1 is bit-identical to its parent. Change 2 is not, because folding a multiply and an add into `v_pk_fma_f32` skips the rounding of the intermediate product: 410363 of 2097152 logits move by at most `3.05e-05` on a `±273` range. Against an fp64 reference the two are equally far from the truth (mean absolute error `4.615302e-04` before, `4.615247e-04` after, identical maxima), because the error floor is the fp8 quantisation of `q` and `k`, not the fp32 epilogue.

All 430 measurement processes across these campaigns were 0-mismatched against the fp32 reference, with no NaN or Inf.

## Testing

Environment: gfx950 (256 CU), ROCm 7.2.4, PyTorch `2.10.0+rocm7.2.4.git3d3aa833`, Triton 3.7.0, one physical GPU pinned per process, clocks not locked.

```bash
# regression module, JIT gluon kernels
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest -q op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py
# -> 62 passed

# the original #5591 repro, unmodified
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=. python repro_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle_false.py
# -> [issue2] allclose=True mismatch=0/6000   (was 5968/6000)
# -> [issue1] no illegal access, exit code 0  (was HIP error 700, exit code 1)

# same repro with AOT loading enabled, after regenerating the artifacts
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS=1 PYTHONPATH=. \
  python repro_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle_false.py
# -> mismatch=0/6000, no illegal access
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS=1 PYTHONPATH=. \
  python -m pytest -q op_tests/test_pa_mqa_logits_offset.py
# -> 2 passed, 60 skipped (the JIT-gated cases skip in AOT mode)
```

The repro script is [PR #5591's file at commit `81d4380`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/81d43801111868be953c360bed9ee60c5e193378/tests/repro_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle_false.py).

Defect 4 was also swept outside pytest with the same shape at cache sizes from 1 MiB to 8 GiB, context pairs `(3001, 513)`, `(3001, 512)`, `(513, 3001)`, `(513, 1025)`, `(3072, 513)` and `(3001,)`, and `TotalCuCount` of 1, 2, 8, 256 and the default: `KVBlockSize=64` and `256` now match the reference everywhere. Before the fix, every case whose first context was not a multiple of the KV block lost the leading logits of the next row.

## Cost of the four fixes

This section predates the two performance sections above and is the cost of the correctness fixes alone, measured before the grid change; its absolutes are not comparable with the numbers there.

Decode, `N=131072`, `H=32`, `D=128`, `next_n=1`, `ChunkK=256`, `WavePerEU=2`, one process per point, median of three, accuracy checked over the whole output on every run.

```bash
# both files in one directory: the fixed test_mqa_logits.py from #5434 (commit
# 849c7c2) for input generation, packing and the FP32 reference, plus the
# driver below
for round in 1 2 3; do
  for batch in 1 16 64 128; do
    for layout in preshuffle plain; do
      ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 PYTHONPATH=. python run_perf.py \
        --batch "$batch" --layout "$layout" --kv-block 64 \
        --output "out/$layout-b$batch-r$round.json"
    done
  done
done
```

Measured on this branch:

| Layout | KVBlock | Batch | KV cache | us | TFLOPS | TB/s | mismatch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 1 | 0.02 GiB | 7.258 | 147.9 | 2.457 | 0/131072 |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 16 | 0.26 GiB | 58.647 | 292.9 | 4.864 | 0/2097152 |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 64 | 1.03 GiB | 274.822 | 250.1 | 4.152 | 0/8388608 |
| Preshuffle=False | 64 | 128 | 2.06 GiB | 470.838 | 291.9 | 4.847 | 0/16777216 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 1 | 0.02 GiB | 5.004 | 214.6 | 3.563 | 0/131072 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 16 | 0.26 GiB | 50.272 | 341.7 | 5.675 | 0/2097152 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 64 | 1.03 GiB | 250.720 | 274.1 | 4.551 | 0/8388608 |
| Preshuffle=True | 64 | 128 | 2.06 GiB | 463.818 | 296.3 | 4.921 | 0/16777216 |
| Preshuffle=True | 256 | 64 | 1.03 GiB | 237.888 | 288.9 | 4.797 | 0/8388608 |
| Preshuffle=True | 256 | 128 | 2.06 GiB | 451.407 | 304.5 | 5.056 | 0/16777216 |

Per-change cost, from paired runs that alternate the two versions within each round. These are deltas only; absolute numbers from different sessions are not comparable, since an unchanged control moved by more than 10% between sessions on this unlocked machine.

Unconditional 64-bit strides in the plain kernel, `KVBlockSize=64`:

| Batch | conditional | unconditional | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.728 | 6.677 | +16.55% |
| 16 | 55.701 | 57.955 | +4.05% |
| 64 | 270.004 | 274.738 | +1.75% |
| 128 | 418.183 | 417.427 | -0.18% |

Batch 128 crosses 2 GiB, so both versions compile the same kernel there; its -0.18% is the noise floor of the setup. With `KVBlockSize=1` the unconditional kernel is faster instead: 247.617 -> 95.281 us at batch 16 and 1053.010 -> 463.740 us at batch 64.

Preshuffle 64-bit addressing and the store bound:

| KVBlock | Batch | before | after | delta | accuracy |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 256 | 64 | 250.599 | 238.254 | -4.93% | 0 -> 0 mismatched |
| 256 | 128 | 449.150 | 451.121 | +0.44% | 508281/16777216 -> 0 |
| 64 | 128 | 464.583 | 463.802 | -0.17% | 0 -> 0 mismatched |

Folding the page base into a `buffer_load` pointer fixes the same addressing but pays a descriptor setup per stage: +4.59% at batch 64 and +3.74% at batch 128, against +0.44% and -4.93% for the global-load form that was kept. Rounds did not overlap between arms, e.g. 247.898/250.599/251.677 before against 238.032/238.254/238.422 after at batch 64.

<details>
<summary>run_perf.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode perf/accuracy driver for one (batch, layout) pair per process.

Reuses the input generation, fp32 reference and packing helpers of the fixed
op_tests/test_mqa_logits.py (PR #5434, commit 849c7c25), and switches both the
KV packing and the interface Preshuffle flag together. Counts mismatches over
the whole output and returns exit code 2 on an accuracy failure.
"""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys

SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "fixed_test_mqa_logits", os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "test_mqa_logits.py")
)
fixed = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
_spec.loader.exec_module(fixed)

import torch  # noqa: E402

from aiter import dtypes  # noqa: E402
from aiter.jit.utils.chip_info import get_gfx  # noqa: E402
from aiter.ops.triton.attention.pa_mqa_logits import (  # noqa: E402
    deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits,
)
from aiter.ops.triton.utils.types import get_fp8_e4m3_dtype  # noqa: E402
from aiter.test_common import run_perftest  # noqa: E402


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--layout", choices=["preshuffle", "plain"], required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=131072)
    parser.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--head-dim", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--next-n", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--kv-block", type=int, default=64)
    parser.add_argument("--chunk-k", type=int, default=256)
    parser.add_argument("--wave-per-eu", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--num-iters", type=int, default=101)
    parser.add_argument("--num-warmup", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if os.path.exists(args.output):
        sys.exit(f"refusing to overwrite {args.output}")

    preshuffle = args.layout == "preshuffle"

    batch, n, heads, dim = args.batch, args.n, args.heads, args.head_dim
    next_n, kv_block = args.next_n, args.kv_block

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    fp8_dtype = get_fp8_e4m3_dtype()

    rows = batch * next_n
    blocks_per_seq = (n + kv_block - 1) // kv_block
    num_blocks = batch * blocks_per_seq

    q = torch.randn(batch, next_n, heads, dim, dtype=dtypes.bf16)
    q_fp8 = q.to(fp8_dtype)
    del q

    kv = torch.randn(num_blocks * kv_block, dim, dtype=dtypes.bf16)
    kv_q, kv_sf = fixed._pertoken_cast_to_fp8(kv, fp8_dtype)
    del kv
    kv_q = kv_q.view(num_blocks, kv_block, dim)
    kv_sf = kv_sf.view(num_blocks, kv_block)

    weights = torch.randn(rows, heads, dtype=dtypes.fp32)
    context_lens = torch.full((batch,), n, dtype=dtypes.i32)
    block_tables = torch.randperm(num_blocks).to(dtypes.i32).view(batch, blocks_per_seq)

    ref, inside = fixed.run_torch_decode(
        q_fp8.float(), kv_q, kv_sf, weights, context_lens, block_tables, n
    )

    kv_cache = fixed._pack_paged_kv(kv_q, kv_sf, preshuffle=preshuffle)
    out_logits = torch.full((rows, n), -float("inf"), dtype=dtypes.fp32)

    def run_triton():
        deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits(
            q_fp8,
            kv_cache,
            weights,
            out_logits,
            context_lens,
            block_tables,
            n,
            Preshuffle=preshuffle,
            KVBlockSize=kv_block,
            ChunkK=args.chunk_k,
            WavePerEU=args.wave_per_eu,
        )
        return out_logits

    total_ctx = int(context_lens.sum().item())
    flops = 2.0 * heads * dim * next_n * total_ctx
    read_bytes = q_fp8.nbytes + total_ctx * (dim + 4) + weights.nbytes
    nbytes = read_bytes + rows * n * 4

    out, us = run_perftest(
        run_triton,
        num_iters=args.num_iters,
        num_warmup=args.num_warmup,
        num_rotate_args=fixed._rotate_args(read_bytes),
    )

    close = torch.isclose(out, ref, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
    mismatch = int((~close).sum().item())
    total = out.numel()
    inside_mismatch = int((~close[inside]).sum().item())
    nan_inf = int((~torch.isfinite(out[inside])).sum().item())

    record = {
        "gfx": get_gfx(),
        "batch": batch,
        "layout": args.layout,
        "n": n,
        "heads": heads,
        "head_dim": dim,
        "next_n": next_n,
        "kv_block": kv_block,
        "chunk_k": args.chunk_k,
        "wave_per_eu": args.wave_per_eu,
        "num_iters": args.num_iters,
        "num_warmup": args.num_warmup,
        "us": us,
        "TFLOPS": flops / us / 1e6,
        "TB/s": nbytes / us / 1e6,
        "mismatch": mismatch,
        "total": total,
        "inside_mismatch": inside_mismatch,
        "inside_total": int(inside.sum().item()),
        "nonfinite_inside": nan_inf,
        "kv_bytes": num_blocks * kv_block * (dim + 4),
        "aot": os.environ.get("AITER_ENABLE_AOT_GLUON_PA_MQA_LOGITS", "0"),
    }
    with open(args.output, "w") as f:
        json.dump(record, f, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    print(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True))

    if mismatch:
        print(f"ACCURACY FAILURE: {mismatch}/{total} mismatched", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

title: [DSv4] Tuned decode moe kernels for mori-EP backend- #41119
body:
## Motivation

Prefill and decode send tokens to very different experts. On DeepSeek-V4 EP8, decode concentrates on a few hot experts, while prefill spreads almost evenly. The same MoE shape therefore wants different kernels in each case.

A single tuned table can't express that. The tuned key uses only the padded token count, and prefill and decode fall into the same buckets. Whichever resolves a bucket first fixes the kernel for both through `get_2stage_cfgs`' `lru_cache`. With CUDA graphs that is always decode, because every bucket is resolved during decode graph capture. The only way to tune decode today is to force the same kernels onto prefill.

This PR lets the caller say whether each call is prefill or decode (the "regime"), and gives each regime its own optional table.

## Summary of changes

- **`aiter/fused_moe.py`**
  - Adds `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE_PREFILL` and `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE_DECODE`, which name a tuned table per regime.
  - Adds `set_moe_regime()`, `get_moe_regime()` and the `moe_regime()` context manager for the host to select the active regime.
  - `get_2stage_cfgs` takes `moe_regime` as an argument, so it becomes part of the cache key. The two regimes get separate cache entries instead of overwriting each other. Both runtime callers (`fused_moe_` and `fused_moe_2stages`) pass the active regime.
  - A regime table replaces the default table but keeps the normal lookup behaviour: activation and tier fallbacks, and the heuristic when a shape is missing. It deliberately does not go through the `config_file=` path, which errors when a shape is missing.
  - When neither env var is set, or the host never sets a regime, behaviour is unchanged and the single `AITER_CONFIG_FMOE` table is used.
- **`aiter/configs/model_configs/moe_regime/dsv4_fp8fp4_ep8_tuned_fmoe_decode.csv`**
  - The decode table for DSV4-Pro FP4 on gfx950 with EP8 and shared-expert fusion (expert=49), token buckets 512 to 16384.
  - Stage1 is tuned against decode's real routing. Stage2 is left on the default geometry.
  - It lives in a subdirectory on purpose. aiter merges every top-level `model_configs/*tuned_fmoe*.csv` into the default table, which would apply the decode kernels to prefill too.
- **`aiter/configs/model_configs/moe_regime/README.md`**
  - Explains that tables in this directory are not merged into the default table, and which env var selects each one.

The host-side change, which sets the regime on each forward pass and pins decode during CUDA graph capture, is in a separate sglang PR.

## Results

Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on 8Ã^W MI355X, ISL/OSL 8k/1k, concurrency 128, DP8/EP8 with MoRI a2a, DSpark MTP.

**Performance**

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Î^T |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 26,468.15 | 27,317.32 | +3.21% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2,940.91 | 3,035.26 | +3.21% |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 39.63 | 38.39 | â^H^R3.14% |
| TPOT median (ms) | 40.91 | 39.47 | â^H^R3.53% |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 43.23 | 42.25 | â^H^R2.28% |

**Accuracy (gsm8k, 200 questions, 5-shot)**

| Metric | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accuracy | 0.960 | 0.965 |
| Invalid | 0.000 | 0.000 |

title: [HIP] feat(custom_ar): add torch.symm_mem transport(mori) for gfx1250
