## Summary

- **torch.symm_mem transport**: Add `torch.distributed._symmetric_memory` (backed by `mori.allocator`) as a new transport for custom all-reduce on gfx1250. Opt-in via `AITER_CUSTOM_AR_USE_SYMM_MEM=1`. Replaces manual IPC handle exchange (TCPStore / Unix socket VMM fd) with `symm_mem.rendezvous()` which handles fabric handles or POSIX fds internally. Reuses existing gfx1250 VMM-style C++ ops (pointer-list interface) — no C++ kernel changes for this part.
- **Collective P2P probe**: Before init, allocates a small buffer + rendezvous across all peers. mori's rendezvous validates P2P via `hipMemSetAccess(RW)` for each peer — all ranks agree on pass/fail, safe fallback to VMM/IPC with no hang risk.
- **world_size 6/8**: Extend gfx1250 template instantiations from {2,4} to {2,4,6,8} across all dispatch points (allreduce, allgather, reduce_scatter). Introduce `DISPATCH_NGPUS_1250` macro to unify the dispatch pattern. No algorithmic changes — kernels are simple `for(i<ngpus)` loops and `Signal`/`RankData` structs already have 8 slots.

title: [JIT] [Build] Make CK fmha kernel generation follow GPU_ARCHS
body:
CK's FMHA codegen was never told which GPU architecture to build for — it either fell back to `gfx9,gfx950`, or was handed a device name it does not recognize, leaving gfx11/gfx12 with no usable FA kernels. This PR derives CK's `--targets` from `GPU_ARCHS` and passes it at every `01_fmha/generate.py` call site.

## Why

Two independent bugs, both silent until dispatch:

- **`mha_recipes._ck_targets_flag()` passed a raw device name** (`gfx1100`) as `--targets`. CK's factory keys are coarser than device names — `gfx11` covers `gfx1100`–`gfx1103` — so it matched nothing, produced an empty kernel set, and `mha_fwd` failed with `invalid argument for fmha_fwd`. **FA did not work on gfx11/gfx12 at all.**
- **Every other call site omitted `--targets`**, so CK fell back to its built-in `gfx9,gfx950` and `GPU_ARCHS` was ignored.

## What changed

203 lines production, 451 tests. Start at `build_targets.py`, then the gates in `mha.py`:

| File | |
|---|---|
| `aiter/jit/utils/build_targets.py` | +69 — the mapping table (§1) |
| `aiter/ops/mha.py` | +100/−23 — call sites and arch gates (§3, the subtle one) |
| `optCompilerConfig.json` · `mha_recipes.py` · `cpp/mha/compile.py` · `core.py` | remaining `--targets` sites (§2) |
| `op_tests/test_ck_fmha_targets*.py` | +339 — no-GPU tests for the table and every gate |

**§1 — Map `GPU_ARCHS` to a CK factory key.**

```
GPU_ARCHS         CK --targets
─────────────────────────────
gfx950       -->  gfx950
gfx125x      -->  gfx125
gfx120x      -->  gfx12
gfx115x      -->  gfx115
gfx11xx      -->  gfx11
other gfx9*  -->  gfx9
unmapped     -->  gfx9,gfx950   (CK's own default — unchanged)
```

`batch_prefill` needs a gfx9-only variant of this, because CK drops *every* batch_prefill kernel if any `--targets` token is not `gfx9*`.

**§2 — Every `generate.py` invocation now passes it**, across the four files that launch it: `optCompilerConfig.json`, the `cmdGenFunc_*` hooks in `mha.py`, `mha_recipes.py`, and the standalone `op_tests/cpp/mha/compile.py`.

**§3 — fp8 / batch_prefill gates, and which arch they read.** fp8 has no CK factory on gfx11/gfx115, and `batch_prefill` is gfx9-only, so both now raise `NotImplementedError` up front instead of failing deep inside CK dispatch.

The catch: `compile_ops` re-runs `gen_func` on **every** call to build its module-name cache key, so the gate sits on the hot path, not just the build path — and it has to read the *live* card, not `GPU_ARCHS`:

```
live call
└── flash_attn_fp8_pertensor_func(...)
    ├── _check_fp8_factory(get_gfx_runtime(), ...)   # public API: the real card
    └── mha_fwd(...)                                  [compile_ops]
        └── _cmdGenFunc_mha_fwd_lookup(...)           # NEW — runs on every call
            ├── _check_fp8_factory(get_gfx_runtime(), ...)
            └── cmdGenFunc_mha_fwd(..., check_build_arch=False)
```

`GPU_ARCHS=gfx942;gfx1100` makes `get_gfx()` return `gfx1100` (last token wins), so gating on `get_gfx()` would reject fp8 on a real gfx942 card. Every production entry point therefore reads `get_gfx_runtime()`: all three `compile_ops` registrations — `mha_fwd`, `mha_varlen_fwd`, `mha_batch_prefill` — go through a `_*_lookup` wrapper that passes `check_build_arch=False`.

`check_build_arch=True` (the default) selects the `get_gfx()` variant for a no-GPU build-time caller. **No such caller exists today** — `setup.py`'s prebuild drives codegen through `get_args_of_build` + `get_mha_varlen_prebuild_variants_by_names` and never calls `cmdGenFunc_*` — so that branch is currently reached only from `test_ck_fmha_targets_wiring.py`. I can drop the parameter if reviewers prefer it gone.

## ⚠️ Behavior change

`GPU_ARCHS="gfx942"` wheels no longer contain gfx950 FA kernels — CK's `gfx9,gfx950` default used to slip them in regardless. **Set `GPU_ARCHS` to every arch the wheel must run on.** `docs/installation.rst` updated.

## Verified

- **No GPU needed** — `op_tests/test_ck_fmha_targets{,_wiring}.py`, 43 passed: the mapping table plus every gate, including the `get_gfx()` / `get_gfx_runtime()` split in §3.
- **gfx1201 (RDNA4)** — 4 new cases in `test_mha.py` pass: hdim-80 pad-up fp16/bf16, fp8bf16 hdim64, fp8bf16 GQA (`max_diff=0.05878` against a `0.07` bound — per-tensor quant noise on the GQA broadcast, not a kernel defect).
- **RDNA coverage, stated plainly** — gfx1201 is the only arch with hardware evidence. gfx1100–1103, gfx1150/1151, gfx1200 and gfx1250 are covered by the mapping-table test only. The new `test_mha.py` cases gate on `_RDNA`/`_GFX12` and skip on the gfx942/gfx950 runners, and `flash_attention_ck` is `if: false` (`.github/workflows/flash_attention_integration.yaml:614-615`), so no CK FA lane exists on any arch today.
- **gfx942/gfx950** — the release default `GPU_ARCHS="gfx942;gfx950"` still maps to `gfx9,gfx950`, byte-identical to CK's old default, so the shipped wheel is unaffected; only single-arch builds narrow (see Behavior change). Leaning on this PR's CI for the regression run.
- `ruff check .` (CI-pinned 0.16.0) and `black --check` clean. No CK change, no submodule bump.

title: [OPUS] Speed up the gfx1250 32mx1 MLA sparse-prefill kernels
body:
## Summary

Rebuilds the two prebuilt gfx1250 code objects that serve `16 < H_Q <= 32` on the DSv4 sparse-prefill path, and reworks the op test so its inputs match how the kernel is actually used in a DSA deployment.

## Kernels

`opus_mla_v4_prefill_a8w8_32mx1_16nx4` now fits two workgroups per CU: LDS drops from 224256 to 157696 bytes (154 KiB, under the 160 KiB half-budget) and the VGPR count from 734 to 512. `opus_mla_v4_prefill_a16w16_32mx1_16nx4` prefetches V one tile ahead in the round loop, trading VGPRs (742 -> 826) for a shorter dependency chain.

Measured with `op_tests/test_pa_sparse_prefill.py --backend opus --h_q 32` across `prec x {1024, 4096} tokens x {1024, 2048} topk x {64Ki, 1Mi} pages`, 16 points per precision:

| precision | min | max | mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bf16 | 1.005x | 1.029x | 1.022x |
| fp8 | 1.077x | 1.300x | 1.207x |

The fp8 gain narrows as the prefix pool grows (1.23-1.30x at 64Ki pages, 1.08-1.19x at 1Mi), which is what an occupancy win looks like once the gather starts missing cache. Accuracy is unchanged: every point reports a 0.0 mismatch ratio against the PyTorch reference.

## Test

The page table now models a DeepSeek Sparse Attention top-k selection instead of uniform-random CSR rows. Each token draws `topk` rows from each range, the extend range is causal (token `i` only sees `[0, i]`, since those rows are the chunk's own K/V), and indices stay scattered so the gather does not degenerate into a near-sequential read. This replaces the `sparse` / `dense` / `empty` modes; `--topk` and `--total_pages` become the sweep axes, with `total_pages` defaulting to `[65536, 1048576]` so the gather is measured outside the caches rather than partly served by L2.

Two hardening changes come with it. Pool rows the page table never names are filled with NaN (0xFF for fp8 NoPE, which is NaN as both e4m3 and E8M0), so a gather that walks off its index list cannot return plausible numbers. The fp8 row pad past the block scales is 0xFF for the same reason. All three backends (`opus`, `triton`, `asm`) pass with both in place.

`_PYTEST_CASES` folds `topk` into each case rather than crossing it as an axis, which kept most combinations from collapsing onto the same whole-pool budget. The seven cases cover every wave layout, both cluster widths, two partial head blocks, a ragged KV tile tail, a whole-pool budget, and empty pools.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Size PS prefill partial buffers from the real token budget

## Motivation

Fixes https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5729.

The MLA PS metadata scheduler returns a pessimistic bound on the max number of partial entries needed to be allocated. This could lead to OOM. The pessimism stems from the fact that it assumed that all requests used the same (maximal) number of query tokens which is not true in inference engines with a fixed query token budget per step.

title: [FlyDSL] Add token-major layout option to GDN prefill h kernel
body:
Summary

Adds an optional token-major layout for the w/u inputs and the v_new output of the FlyDSL gated-delta-rule hidden-state kernel chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h_flydsl_opt. New public param wu_head_major: bool = True on the host wrapper (aiter/ops/flydsl/linear_attention_prefill_kernels.py); when False, w/u are consumed token-major ([B,T,H,D]) and v_new is stored token-major ([B,T,H,V]). Default True preserves the existing head-major behavior exactly. Implemented via a compile-time const_expr branch in the device kernel (aiter/ops/flydsl/kernels/gdr_prefill/chunk_gated_delta_h.py), so the head-major path is unchanged.

Motivation: lets a consumer with native token-major GDN tensors (e.g. SGLang's linear-attention path) reach the kernel without a transpose.

Technical Details

- Head-major path is provably unchanged: emitted ISA is byte-identical between base and this branch (same VGPR/occupancy). Zero regression by construction (compile-time dead-branch elimination).
- Correctness: token-major output is bit-exact against the head-major reference on dense and production varlen shapes, including an unaligned tail.
- wu_head_major=False changes both the v_new store base/stride and the w/u input loads, which move from head-major ([B,H,T,D], token-row stride D) to token-major ([B,T,H,D], token-row stride H*D) — see chunk_gated_delta_h.py:394-400. K/V stays the unit-stride innermost dimension in both layouts, so lane-level coalescing is unchanged; the difference is inter-token-row locality (head-major advances 256 B/row for K=V=128 BF16, token-major advances H·256 B/row).
- Performance is layout- and architecture-dependent, not neutral. On gfx950 (CDNA4, the target arch) token-major is within noise to slightly faster. On gfx942 (CDNA3) token-major measures ~4.3% slower (dense T=1024) and ~6.1% slower (varlen 8×1024) than head-major, from the reduced token-row spatial locality above (a secondary cache/prefetch effect, not a coalescing failure). For a consumer with native token-major tensors, the saved host transpose can still make wu_head_major=False a net win; on gfx942 it is a trade-off to weigh against the transpose cost.

AOT / prebuild

The FlyDSL AOT enumeration (aiter/aot/flydsl/chunk_gdn_h.py) now fans out wu_contig over both values with layout-matched compile dummies, so the token-major specialization is prebuilt into the packaged cache rather than cold-JIT-compiling on the first wu_head_major=False serving-path call. Verified on gfx950: enumeration count doubles (288 → 576 jobs, 288 head-major + 288 token-major), and a fresh-process token-major call under FLYDSL_RUNTIME_RUN_ONLY=1 (which forbids compile-on-miss) hits the prebuilt cache — with an empty-cache negative control raising the expected "no usable AOT cache" error, confirming the hit depends on the prebuilt artifact and not a JIT fallback.

Test Plan

- op_tests/test_flydsl_linear_attention_prefill.py runs a direct token-major == head-major torch.equal exact assertion (on h, layout-normalized v_new, and final_state) on every case in the default sweep.
- Default run also exercises two dedicated review cases: review-unaligned-varlen (varlen T=1000, a non-multiple-of-BT=64 tail) and review-dense-b2 (dense_batch=2, token-major dense base path).
- ISA diff of the head-major path between base and this branch.

Test Result

- Bit-exact match (torch.equal) between token-major and head-major outputs on all tested shapes, including the unaligned-tail and dense_batch>1 cases, on gfx950.
- Identical emitted ISA (VGPR/occupancy) for the head-major path, confirming no regression.

Submission Checklist

- [x] Default behavior (wu_head_major=True) unchanged
- [x] New path validated bit-exact against reference (direct token-major == head-major torch.equal assertion)
- [x] Token-major specialization AOT-prebuilt (no cold-JIT serving stall)
- [x] Performance characterized per architecture (gfx950 neutral/faster; gfx942 ~4–6% slower

title: [HIP] opt inverse rope group quant gfx1250
body:
## Motivation

Follows #4806. The payload now goes through the gfx1250 tensor engine, the
tier orders apply to row-major, and the op carries one stated policy for
non-finite input. Also fixes an out-of-bounds LDS write, a SIGABRT that
#4806's layout gate introduced, and a dispatch band that was removed by
mistake

## Technical Details

1. Tier sort extended to row-major narrow slices. The orders were restricted
to n32k4, but row-major admits the same sort and it is worth 13-18% once
the slice is narrow. The gain is the narrow quantize path -- a pass whose
groups all miss the rotary tail needs no widening, no cos/sin and no f32 --
which only a uniform segment per wave can select statically. Gated on
TDS == 16: below that a wave spans too few groups to amortize the sort.
2. Payload staged through the tensor engine. Every access order this kernel
uses is a regular 2D tile, tiering included, so the window is
dim0 = run*GROUP_SIZE by dim1 = slots/run and the tier only moves the
origin. Most of the effect is the staged wait: s_wait_tensorcnt<0>
serialises every tile behind the first consumer.
3. WAR stalls removed. s_wait_xcnt was 45% of all stall cycles in the s=16384
ATT trace -- three exec-mask writes landing on a store still in flight:
store_scale's saveexec around a one-byte store whose lanes already agree on
address and value, the cos/sin load's lane-term guard, and a wave-uniform
tdm_wave that divergence analysis could not see through.
4. Four-group heads tier at the exact cut. At GS=128 rope lives only in group
3, so cutting at GROUPS_PER_HEAD/2 filed the pure-nope group 2 under rope
and it paid f32 widening for a rotation it never performs. Held to four
groups per head; the same correction at eight costs 11.7%.

Each scale layout is built only where it can run. mfma_tile feeds CDNA's
V_MFMA_SCALE and n32k4 feeds RDNA's WMMA scaleB, so a third of the module
was kernels the target could never launch.
  gfx1250   372 -> 264 instantiations, 5.31 -> 3.88 MiB device code
  gfx950    372 -> 264 instantiations, 5.31 -> 3.27 MiB device code
  build     26.6 -> 22.3 s
The gate lives entirely in the translation unit; both macros keep an
#ifndef escape hatch for a target that genuinely needs both.


## Test Plan

384 checks pass on gfx1250, HIP graph capture/replay included. gfx942 is
added to SUPPORTED_GFX: its exclusion cited permlane16_swap, which the amax
reduction stopped using, and the op builds and runs there with mfma_tile
included.
Two gaps the sweep could not reach are now covered. Rows whose Ks leaves a
part-wave block, at 9 and 3 heads -- every default shape is a whole number
of waves. And the invalid-group policy, since none of the DATA_DISTS can
produce a non-finite input, which is why that behaviour had moved twice
under optimisation with nothing watching it.

## Test Result

gfx1250, h,g = 128,16, against main. Four interleaved rounds -- both builds
measured inside each round, since absolute timings drift between batches and
only a ratio taken within a round holds up. Median of the per-round ratios:
                          main      branch
  row   GS=128  s=2048   36.18 us   24.89 us   -31.2%
  row   GS=128  s=16384 295.59 us  211.08 us   -28.6%
  row   GS=32   s=2048   35.93 us   27.04 us   -24.7%
  row   GS=128  s=512     7.99 us    6.27 us   -21.3%
  row   GS=32   s=16384 293.00 us  237.78 us   -18.8%
  n32k4 GS=32   s=2048   33.12 us   29.86 us    -9.8%
  n32k4 GS=32   s=16384 261.91 us  238.36 us    -8.9%
The two remaining s=512 points, row/GS=32 and n32k4/GS=32, land around -5%
but spread several points round to round, so they are quoted that way rather
than to a figure.
A wider sweep -- 2 head configs x 3 layout/group-size combinations x 6
values of S -- is uniformly in the same direction with no regression, but it
was collected one build after the other and so carries that batch drift;
treat it as direction rather than magnitude.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

title: [CK] [Bugfix][Perf] fused_moe: tune the non-temporal load hint per tuned row
body:
## What's wrong

`get_2stage_cfgs()` initialises the non-temporal load hint to `False` and assigns it only
inside the heuristic branch:

```python
use_non_temporal_load = False
if cfg is None or bypass_tuned_config:
    use_non_temporal_load = use_nt(token, topk, expert)   # heuristic branch only
else:
    ...                                                   # tuned branch: never assigned
```

A shape loses non-temporal weight loads the moment it gains a tuned CSV row, and
`AITER_USE_NT` is dead there as well, because the override lives inside `use_nt()`.

An earlier revision of this PR simply derived the flag on the tuned path too. Review pointed
out why that is not sound, and measurements agree: the tuner never passes `non_temporal_load`
(`gemm_moe_tune.py` -> `ck_moe_stage{1,2}_fwd_out`), so **every** candidate in every shipped
row was ranked with the hint off. Turning it on at runtime runs the selected kernel outside
the conditions it was selected in, and the recorded `us1`/`us2` stop describing runtime. On
gfx942 that shows up directly: the shipped `ds_v3` row for `7168x2048 e33 topk9` at token 128
(`block_m=32`) is **6.6 % slower** with the hint on, while the same shape at tokens 16 and 64
is 5.0 % / 3.5 % faster. One shape family, no constant right answer.

## Fix

Make the hint part of what gets tuned instead of something derived next to the tuned row. The
tuner sweeps both values for the quant types whose kernels read it, ranks
`(kernel, block_m, nt)` jointly by `us1 + us2`, and records the winner in a new `nt` column;
the runtime reads that column.

```diff
     else:
         block_m = cfg["block_m"]
+        # rows tuned before the nt column keep the hint off
+        nt_override = int(os.environ.get("AITER_USE_NT", "-1"))
+        if nt_override != -1:
+            use_non_temporal_load = bool(nt_override)
+        elif "nt" in cfg:
+            use_non_temporal_load = bool(int(cfg["nt"]))
```

`use_nt()` and the heuristic branch are untouched, so nothing changes for shapes without a
tuned row. Rows without the column keep `nt=False`, which is today's behaviour, so no shipped
config changes until it is retuned. `AITER_USE_NT` now overrides both paths, as it was
documented to. On the tuner side `nt` is threaded exactly like the existing `flat` / `xbf16`
columns: it rides in the candidate tag, becomes a column in the candidate table, joins the
dedup key and the stage1 x stage2 merge key (so both stages of a row agree on it), and is
written out. The sweep is gated to `per_1x128`, so every other quant type keeps its candidate
count.

## Results, MI325X (gfx942, 304 CU)

DSv3 EP shape `7168x2048 e33 topk9`, per_1x128 fp8 blockscale, preshuffled weights.

**Tuner level** — same box, same harness, the extra dimension is the only difference:

| token | without the nt sweep    | with the nt sweep               | gain   |
| ----- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------ |
| 16    | `block_m=16`, 360.34 us | `block_m=16`, `nt=1`, 329.59 us | +8.5 % |
| 64    | `block_m=32`, 375.48 us | `block_m=32`, `nt=1`, 358.88 us | +4.4 % |
| 128   | `block_m=64`, 404.58 us | `block_m=64`, `nt=1`, 395.84 us | +2.2 % |

**Runtime level** — whole `fused_moe` op, CUDA-graph replay, 200 iters after 40 warmup, 8
rotated weight sets, 3 interleaved rounds per config, median:

| token | shipped rows | retuned, no nt sweep | retuned, nt swept | vs shipped |
| ----- | ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| 16    | 383.2 us     | 374.5 us             | 329.6 us          | +14.0 %    |
| 64    | 398.0 us     | 411.5 us             | 365.0 us          | +8.3 %     |
| 128   | 455.4 us     | 431.2 us             | 417.2 us          | +8.4 %     |

Retuning with the hint in the search is worth +3.3 % to +12.0 % over retuning without it on
the same box.

**Why this cannot be a heuristic.** The `block_m` the tuner picks and the best value of the
hint are coupled: what the hint discards is weight reuse between M-tiles of the same expert,
so it wins while an expert stays inside one tile and loses once it spans two. At token 128 on
this shape, stage2 measured alone with `rocprofv3` is 161.0 -> 191.8 us with the hint at
`block_m=32`, but 153.1 -> 135.7 us at `block_m=64`; `rocprofv3 --pmc TCC_HIT_sum TCC_MISS_sum`
attributes the whole difference to cache hit rate (42.8 % -> 28.5 %, 722 MB -> 920 MB below L2
against 2 x 484 MB of logical B reads, both arms sustaining ~4 TB/s). A predicate over token
count cannot see `block_m`, and under imbalanced routing it cannot see the tail experts that
cross into a second tile before the mean does either. Tuning it removes the guesswork.

## Results, MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU)

Second architecture, independent box. 26 shapes from three families (`4096x384 e128 topk8`,
`7168x512 e257 topk9`, `3072x1536 e256 topk8`), same machine, same harness, same
single-process settings, one card, tuned **three times per arm** at the PR's parent `c3caa55`
and at the head `c26f391`. 23 of the 26 resolve a winner on every run of both arms (the other
three are under *Caveats*). Times are the tuner's own per-candidate measurement for the
winning row; gain is median-of-three, spread is max-min within an arm.

The result separates by winning path. The 16 asm 1-stage shapes do not read the flag and do
not move: all keep `nt=0`, median gain +0.07 % over a range of -0.7 % .. +0.8 % against
per-arm spreads up to 1.4 %. The 7 CK 2-stage shapes are one family, `4096x384 e128 topk8`,
`doweight_stage1=1`, all at `block_m=16`:

| token | parent    | PR        | gain   | per-arm spread | `nt`                |
| ----- | --------- | --------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------------- |
| 1     | 38.62 us  | 38.19 us  | +1.1 % | 7.1 % / 4.6 %  | `0`/`1`, unstable   |
| 2     | 42.65 us  | 41.38 us  | +3.0 % | 6.2 % / 1.5 %  | `1`                 |
| 4     | 50.69 us  | 47.30 us  | +6.7 % | 6.2 % / 3.6 %  | `1`                 |
| 8     | 61.86 us  | 57.14 us  | +7.6 % | 1.3 % / 2.7 %  | `1`                 |
| 16    | 83.12 us  | 76.54 us  | +7.9 % | 1.4 % / 1.7 %  | `1`                 |
| 32    | 113.93 us | 105.10 us | +7.8 % | 0.3 % / 0.4 %  | `1`                 |
| 64    | 122.32 us | 113.05 us | +7.6 % | 0.2 % / 0.4 %  | `1`                 |

From token 8 up, the gain is several times either arm's spread and holds within half a point
across four shapes. At tokens 1-4 the shape runs in tens of microseconds, the arms overlap,
and token 1 does not even settle on a value across repeats — the flag genuinely does not
matter there, so nothing is claimed. Both arms pick the same kernel pair at tokens 1-16; at
tokens 32 and 64 the PR arm's winner is the `128x16x128x128` variant rather than
`256x16x128x256`, which is the ranking doing its job once `nt` is in the search space. An
isolated single-shape rerun where both arms converged on the identical kernel and `block_m`
isolates the flag on its own: 121.76 us -> 114.31 us, +6.1 % (stage1 +7.0 %, stage2 +4.5 %).


## Cost and compatibility

* CK candidates double for `per_1x128` only: 10 -> 20 per shape here, one shape 19 s -> 38 s,
  roughly 10 min for a full model file. Verified that a `per_Token` tune is unchanged.
* Rows without the column behave exactly as today. The 46 shipped blockscale 2-stage rows with
  `use_nt() == True` (38 at `cu_num` 256, 8 at `cu_num` 304) keep the hint off until someone
  retunes them; retuning shipped configs is out of scope here.
* No C++ change: `ck_moe_stage{1,2}_fwd` already take the flag and `gen_instances.py` already
  compiles both NT instantiations.

## Verification

* Runtime decision table, all five cases checked against `get_2stage_cfgs` on **both** gfx942
  and gfx950: legacy CSV (no column) -> off; `nt=0` -> off; `nt=1` -> on; legacy +
  `AITER_USE_NT=1` -> on; `nt=1` + `AITER_USE_NT=0` -> off. At the parent commit all five
  return off, which is the bug.
* Shipped-config regression, exhaustive: all **179** `cu_num=256` blockscale 2-stage rows across
  the 7 shipped CSVs (`ds_v3`, `glm5`, `minimax-m2_5`, `qwen3_235b`, `qwen3_5_397b`, and the
  untuned files) resolved through `get_2stage_cfgs` on both arms and compared field by field —
  `block_m`, `ksplit`, both kernel names, `nt_stage1`, `nt_stage2`. **Zero differences.** 119 of
  those rows are ones where `use_nt()` would return `True`; they stay off on both arms,
  confirming the heuristic was already inert on the tuned path and that this change does not
  switch it on.
* Tuner smoke test: the dispatch list shows each CK kernel twice, once per value; the candidate
  table and the tuned CSV carry `nt`; `per_Token` keeps its candidate count.
* Hand-written rows confirm the column drives the kernel: the same shipped config with `nt=1`
  reproduces +5.0 % / +3.5 % / -6.6 % at tokens 16 / 64 / 128.
* Numerics: the flag only selects `AmdBufferCoherenceEnum`, no arithmetic changes. Measured on
  gfx950, per-candidate reference error is identical between the two arms and between `nt=0` and
  `nt=1` (stage1 0.1 % in every group; stage2 within 0.1 pp).
* `op_tests/test_moe_blockscale.py` exits 0 with the same six checks; instrumenting
  `get_2stage_cfgs` shows it never enters the tuned branch (asm path only), so it does not cover
  this change.
* `ruff` clean on both files; no new findings (3 pre-existing in the tuner, 34 pre-existing E501
  in `fused_moe.py`, unchanged).

## Caveats

* The rankings above were produced with the catastrophic-mismatch check relaxed locally, because
  the tuner's reference comparison rejects blockscale stage1 candidates — asm and CK alike — on
  both of my boxes, while `per_Token` is unaffected. That blocks blockscale tuning independently
  of this change: the two files involved are untouched by this PR, and the parent commit fails
  identically on the same shapes. On gfx950 it is what leaves the three shapes above unresolved.
  The measurements are unaffected, since both arms are gated identically and the per-candidate
  errors match between them.
* Per-stage tuning of the hint is deliberately not attempted: the runtime passes one flag to both
  stages, so the merge forces stage1 and stage2 of a row to agree.

## Duplicate check

This updates my own #5443. Of the 640 open PRs, none touch `use_nt` / `non_temporal_load` in
`aiter/fused_moe.py`: #5117 is MXFP6 non-temporal *stores* in GEMM, #2947 is a gfx942 CK stage2
OOB fix, #3493 adds gfx942 tuned rows (12 more `cu_num=304` blockscale 2-stage rows, all of which
this PR leaves at `nt=0` until retuned).

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: Feature/minimax m3 mxfp8
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 dense MXFP8 on gfx950 stores B in the MX-scale preshuffle layout. The Triton path has to reshape those tensors first. This PR adds a FlyDSL GEMM that consumes packed A, shuffled B, and MX scales as they sit in the checkpoint, plus the MiniMax-M3 TP4 tune table so those signatures dispatch.

Fused MoE EP lookup still has two key conventions: routed top-k, and routed top-k plus a fake slot. Callers that pass the real width need to select that key instead of matching topk-1.

## Technical Details
Five commits:
1. FlyDSL MX-scale preshuffle GEMM — gfx950 kernel, host dispatch, AOT, and minimax_m3_dense_mxfp8_mxscale_preshuffle_tuned_gemm.csv (147 fp8×fp8 rows, M=1…16384, MiniMax TP4 NKs such as 1536/2560×6144).
2. has_fake_topk_slot on fused MoE — default EP lookup still tries the historical fake-slot key, then the runtime width. False uses the routed width only. Same flag on fused_moe / fused_moe_ / fhmoe.
3. Tuner at op_tests/tuners/tune_mxscale_preshuffle.py; tile catalog under ops/flydsl/gemm_tune/.
4. GPU sweep at op_tests/test_flydsl_mxscale_preshuffle.py (2D contiguous host contract).
5. Kernel cleanup — gpu.thread_id / block_id to i32 at first use; split-K bf16 pack via .to() instead of arith.trunc_f.

Kernel, dispatch, tuner, and EP lookup were written from FlyDSL GEMM / translation rules and the AMD GPU authoring contract (gfx950, AITER harness, correctness before a win), then checked in a separate review pass (Index types, layouts, lookup keys, tests). Companion SGLang wiring is not in this PR.

## Test Plan

- CPU: pytest op_tests/test_fused_moe_config_lookup.py op_tests/tuning_tests/test_csv_validation.py op_tests/tuning_tests/test_config_shape_collision.py -k 'mxscale or fused_moe or no_duplicates'
- GPU (gfx950): python op_tests/test_flydsl_mxscale_preshuffle.py (and -s 1,2560,6144 4,1536,6144)
- Tuner (optional): python op_tests/tuners/tune_mxscale_preshuffle.py

## Test Result

- After rebase onto origin/main: 23 CPU tests passed (MoE lookup + CSV/collision). All 147 tuned rows have errRatio=0.0.
- GPU sweep is op_tests/test_flydsl_mxscale_preshuffle.py (checkAllclose vs dequant + F.linear). Run that on gfx950 before merge.

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#pull-requests.

title: [FlyDSL] Refactor PA decode and load CSV tuning results
body:
Refactor the monolithic FlyDSL PA decode kernel into operation classes following `fmha_gfx950`, and let the PA interface consume offline workgroup-budget recommendations from CSV.

- Split schedule/traits, context, memory movement, GEMM, softmax, epilogue, and pipeline components. Carry forward dense planned query splitting, eligible unsigned FP8 buffer addressing between 2 and 4 GiB, K/V prefetch scheduling, and compact/window-bounded reductions.
- Store complete tuning results in one CSV: readable shape/budget/performance columns plus structured payload cells preserve raw timing samples, accuracy checks, failures, and source fingerprints. Loading validates the row hierarchy and displayed values. `--output results.csv` is the output path; `--csv` is an alias. Dry-run output is also CSV.
- Add `load_tuned_results()` to the PA interface. It caches an immutable index of validated recommendations, checks current source fingerprints, and rejects ambiguous recommendations for the same device-local geometry. The default path is `aiter/configs/model_configs/flydsl_pa_decode_tuned.csv`; an absent default gives no recommendations. Explicit missing or malformed files raise an error, and `reload=True` refreshes the index.

Omitting `max_context_partition_num` and `work_plan` enables automatic eager planning:

```python
pa_decode(
    ...,
    max_context_partition_num=None,
    tuned_file="results.csv",
    max_context_length=max_context_length,
)
```

The host context bound and local tensor geometry select the recommendation. Missing, stale, conflicting, or unmatched recommendations use the default budget of `2 * CU`; attention with sinks also uses the default because the tuner measures attention without sinks. The host bound controls page-rounded planned scheduling, so padded block tables retain the measured query-splitting policy. Callers must ensure GPU context lengths do not exceed that bound; matching does not read lengths back from the GPU.

Explicit integer partition counts retain static execution. Explicit work plans take precedence and can supply their partition cap when the argument is omitted. For graph capture or preallocated scratch, load the CSV and use `results.lookup_budget(shape, architecture, num_cu)` to prepare a plan before capture, then pass `work_plan` and the matching context bound. Automatic planning is rejected during capture.

Validation of the CSV/API change:

- 62 CPU checks pass, covering complete CSV roundtrips, malformed/truncated/duplicate data, CLI output, atomic replacement, cache/reload behavior, immutable results, source/accuracy rejection, and local-shape conflicts. These harnesses exercise the actual codec and loader definitions without GPU imports.
- 144 independent offline scheduling-bound checks pass across page sizes 16/64/128 and automatic, explicit-plan, and static modes. The gfx950 B4/QL4/G16/D128/L4096/budget256 example selects identical complete schedules for compact and padded tables when given the same host bound.
- Black, Ruff, and diff checks pass. `op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_decode.py` adds 11 host test cases and two GPU integration cases for automatic planning, fallback, padded tables, explicit-plan precedence, and graph replay. The existing 242 native cases are retained.
- **GPU validation of this update remains unexecuted:** all eight available remote MI355 devices retained other workloads, and the local gfx942 probe blocked in HIP initialization before PA/FlyDSL code ran. No new GPU accuracy, throughput, or regression result is claimed. Frozen snapshots, verified source manifests, and guarded accuracy/performance launchers are prepared for a rerun.

The kernel operation files are unchanged by the CSV/API update. Earlier validation at `a24ea4967`, against the optimized monolithic implementation `7f3d014cd`, passed 242/242 native cases on each revision. Across 35 offline gfx950/gfx942 tile specializations, location-stripped MLIR, complete HSACO, and register/LDS/spill metadata matched. gfx942 coverage in that comparison was offline only.

The earlier MI355/gfx950 target comparison used batch 200, QL4, Hkv1/G16, D128, page128, transposed V, BF16 Q/output, per-token FP8 KV, and contexts from 4 to 200000:

| Workgroup budget | Monolithic `7f3d014cd` median (µs) | Validated `a24ea4967` median (µs) | Validated logical KV TB/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 1135.582 | 1139.307 | 4.494 |
| 2048 | 973.574 | 973.608 | **5.259** |

Each row is a separate paired run. Timing includes decode and reduction and excludes loading/planning, JIT, allocation, quantization, and reference calculation. Logical KV throughput counts 5,120,077,056 K+V bytes once per call, without a QL multiplier, using `bytes / (median_us * 1e6)`.

**Known precision limitation from that comparison:** `varlen_b81_q4_c1027` (batch 81, QL4, Hkv1/G16, D128/page128, per-token FP8 KV, contexts 4–1027) fails the strict FP32-reference check at `atol=rtol=0.005` on both validated revisions: 38 elements exceed tolerance, with maximum absolute error 0.00712435. Outputs are byte-identical. This failure was retained and excluded from timing; tolerances were not changed.

title: [HIP] [FlyDSL] [JIT] Support Conv3d for Qwen-Image / Wan2.1 VAE on MI35X
body:
## Motivation

aiter has no conv3d (only Triton conv2d). Two diffusion VAEs need one:

- **Wan2.1** encodes in 4-frame chunks and prepends 2 cached feature frames
  after the first chunk. Those frames are real, not causal-pad zeros, so the
  `T=1` `conv3d -> conv2d` identity fails. That is **67.7% of one encode's 650
  convolution calls**.
- **Qwen-Image** is the same VAE fine-tuned at `T=1`, where the identity holds,
  so it needs this kernel's 2-D path.

A GEMM library cannot absorb these shapes: N is the 96/192/384 channel ladder,
and 7 of 18 Qwen-Image shapes have `K` not a multiple of 64 or `N=3`, which
A16W16 cannot express.

## Technical Details

### 1. Vendored implicit-GEMM convolution (`flydsl_conv_implicit`)

Same vendoring as `gemm_a16w16_gfx950`. Dispatches 1D/2D/3D off filter rank;
gathers from the source instead of im2col (~9× less activation traffic).
Keyword surface unchanged (`groups`, `padding_mode`, `splitk`, `stream`,
`tile`, `wgm`, `autotune`, `input_layout`, `output_layout`).

Three mechanical edits vs upstream: local `buffer_atomic_add` (flydsl wheel
has no `kernels/common/`); `kt` -> `k_tile` (filter temporal extent); one
`if` collapsed to `and`. 54/56 top-level definitions byte-identical.

Named `flydsl_conv_implicit` because the entry point dispatches on rank.

### 2. Offline tile tuner

The heuristic N tiles are powers of two. Against 96/192/384, two rungs sit at
**75% N occupancy**; masked B columns still issue MFMA. `TILE_N` 96/192 is
legal but was unreachable: `TILE_{M,N} % (16 * WAVE_M * WAVE_N) == 0` excludes
the eight-wave shape every shipped candidate uses.

- `conv3d_policy.py` enumerates that closed form (reject = arithmetic, not a
  compile), then prunes on N fill, waves, LDS, accumulators.
- `csrc/flydsl_conv3d/conv3d_tune.py` writes per-model CSVs under
  `aiter/configs/model_configs/` (`qwenimage_vae_*`, `wan21_vae_*`).
- `_lookup_tuned_tile` reads them. Miss / missing file / malformed row falls
  back to the unmodified heuristic.

Launch config is five integers, not a `solidx` (reordering candidates must not
silently invalidate the table).

**Tune with `--compare --update_improved`.** `mp_tuner` times across eight GPU
processes; production runs one. A bare sweep regressed three shapes by up to
4.8%. The compare gate re-times on the production path and rejects gains below
`--min_improvement_pct` (default 3%).

Also fixes `autotune=True` / `FLYDSL_CONV3D_AUTOTUNE=1`, which imported a
FlyDSL-repo path and raised `ImportError`.

### 3. A16W16 pruner fix

`GemmConfigPruner` `keep_ratio` climbs with M: at M=27556 it kept only tiles
wasting <0.44% on padding. HTI needs `block_n=256`, so N=384 (pad to 512)
dropped the whole HTI catalog (~30% loss). Cap lets a tile pad up to 30%.

### 4. Tests

`op_tests/test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py`: keyword surface plus Wan / Qwen
shapes from an input resolution (`--wan-res`, `--wan-frames`, `--qwen-res`),
traced on meta-device encodes. Benches:
`op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_three_way.py` (conv vs
A16W16 vs hipBLASLt) and `bench_conv_tuned_ab.py` (tile table on vs off).

## Test Plan

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py
python3 -m unittest op_tests.tuning_tests.test_config_shape_collision -v

PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 csrc/flydsl_conv3d/conv3d_tune.py \
  -i aiter/configs/model_configs/qwenimage_vae_bf16_untuned_conv3d.csv \
  -o aiter/configs/model_configs/qwenimage_vae_bf16_tuned_conv3d.csv \
  --max_configs 32 --mp 8 --compare --update_improved

PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_three_way.py
PYTHONPATH=$PWD python3 op_tests/op_benchmarks/flydsl/qwenimage_vae_conv/bench_conv_tuned_ab.py
```

All results below: gfx950 / 256 CU, bf16.

## Test Result

### Correctness

`test_flydsl_conv_implicit.py`: **75/75 `checkAllclose`**, `rtol=atol=2e-2`.
`flydsl err` **0 on all 33 model shapes** (the one non-zero cell is torch's
own bf16 rounding at K=27, `err_ratio` 4e-05).

`test_config_shape_collision.py`: 18/18, including `conv3d_bf16_tuned`.

Every tuned row has `err_ratio = 0.0`. Instrumenting `_lookup_tuned_tile`
over the op_test: **1236 hits / 12 distinct shapes**, all non-default tiles
(e.g. `(96, 96, 2, 3)`, `(192, 128, 2, 2)`, `(128, 192, 1, 4) wgm=8`).

### Performance (gfx950 / 256 CU, bf16)

One table for the published buckets. **vs X** is `X_ms / current CSV` (or
`torch / orig flydsl` only where current is missing). Torch and original
flydsl † are the PR-open three-way (NCHW, includes pre-transpose). hip is
`three_way.json` library-best `torch.mm` on materialised `M×K` (no im2col).
Current CSV is NDHWC (`ed7b5a5a8`). ‡ NCDHW-tuned CSV (`05f919868`). Mixed
sessions; hip/a16 traffic is not the conv gather.

| bucket | torch | orig flydsl | hip | current CSV | vs orig flydsl | vs hip | vs torch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan2.1 `T>1`/cached, 480×832, 81f (8 shapes, 440 calls) | 505.32 ms | 310.37 ms † | — | **200.91 ms** | **1.55x** | — | **2.52x** |
| Wan2.1 same 8, 368×544, 81f | — | 128.70 ms ‡ | — | **110.43 ms** | **1.17x** | — | — |
| Qwen-Image, 1024² (10 shapes, 52 calls) | 20.37 ms | 12.00 ms † | 8.70 ms | **7.76 ms** | **1.55x** | **1.12x** | **2.63x** |
| Qwen-Image, 1024² (16 layers, 58 calls) | — | — | 10.02 ms | **8.92 ms** | — | **1.12x** | — |
| Qwen-Image, 1328² (10 shapes, 52 calls) | — | 16.13 ms ‡ | — | **12.68 ms** | **1.27x** | — | — |
| Wan2.1 resamplers + pointwise (15 shapes) | 34.67 ms | 32.07 ms † | — | — | — | — | 1.08x † |

† Three-way at PR open (NCHW in). Orig flydsl vs torch on that row is **1.63x**
(Wan 8-shape) / **1.70x** (Qwen 10-shape) / **1.08x** (resamplers). Wan conv3d
matches the Lumen 81-frame report (1.59x). Minus the two `time_conv`, the
pointwise bucket is 0.99x (stay on torch); `time_conv` alone is 1.54x
(`3x1x1`, `K=C*3`). `time_conv` is not in the tuned tables, so the 15-shape
row has no current CSV. Hip was not measured for Wan T>1 (A up to ~8 GB,
omits 27× im2col). Qwen 1328² hip exists for only 2 of 10 shapes.

CSV rows outside those buckets (same weighting):

| | resample 3×3 (6 shapes, 63 calls) | decode extras (8 shapes, 103 calls) | all CSV rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wan 480×832 | 6.69 ms | 41.88 ms | 249.49 ms (22 shapes, 606 calls) |
| Wan 368×544 | 4.02 ms | 21.92 ms | 136.36 ms |
| Qwen 1024², 16 layers (adds 3 downs + 3 ups) | — | — | 8.92 ms (58 calls) |
| Qwen 1328², 16 layers | — | — | 14.63 ms |

#### Wan2.1 `T>1`/cached conv3d, weighted (81 frames)

| shape | calls | 480×832 `us` | 480 contrib | 368×544 `us` | 368 contrib |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `conv_in` 3→96 | 20 | 183.46 | 3.67 ms | 114.62 | 2.29 ms |
| `down_0_1` 96→96 | 80 | 1017.87 | 81.43 ms | 515.87 | 41.27 ms |
| `down_3_in` 96→192 | 20 | 469.12 | 9.38 ms | 245.18 | 4.90 ms |
| `down_3_4` 192→192 | 60 | 907.95 | 54.48 ms | 467.67 | 28.06 ms |
| `down_6_in` 192→384 | 20 | 226.62 | 4.53 ms | 128.58 | 2.57 ms |
| `down_6_7` 384→384 | 60 | 456.06 | 27.36 ms | 247.35 | 14.84 ms |
| `down_9_10_mid` 384→384 | 160 | 114.82 | 18.37 ms | 92.70 | 14.83 ms |
| `conv_out` 384→32 | 20 | 84.46 | 1.69 ms | 82.91 | 1.66 ms |
| **weighted** | **440** | | **200.91 ms** | | **110.43 ms** |

#### Qwen-Image conv2d, weighted (one encode+decode)

| shape | calls | 1024² `us` | 1024 contrib | 1328² `us` | 1328 contrib |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `3->96` | 1 | 93.65 | 0.09 ms | 139.86 | 0.14 ms |
| `96->96` | 10 | 262.65 | 2.63 ms | 439.36 | 4.39 ms |
| `96->192` | 1 | 122.02 | 0.12 ms | 195.23 | 0.20 ms |
| `192->192` | 9 | 202.00 | 1.82 ms | 343.49 | 3.09 ms |
| `192->384` | 2 | 104.61 | 0.21 ms | 173.29 | 0.35 ms |
| `384->384` (L2) | 8 | 189.34 | 1.51 ms | 319.24 | 2.55 ms |
| `384->384` (L3) | 18 | 65.50 | 1.18 ms | 91.20 | 1.64 ms |
| `384->32` | 1 | 31.14 | 0.03 ms | 32.50 | 0.03 ms |
| `16->384` | 1 | 15.92 | 0.02 ms | 18.90 | 0.02 ms |
| `96->3` | 1 | 145.26 | 0.15 ms | 262.38 | 0.26 ms |
| **weighted** | **52** | | **7.76 ms** | | **12.68 ms** |

#### Per-shape vs hipBLASLt `mm` and FlyDSL `gemm_a16w16` (same `M/N/K`)

hip / a16 from `three_way.json`. **vs hip** = `hip_us / other_us`. a16 is `—`
when `K % 64 != 0` or `N=3` (7/18 shapes). `@166²` is 1328² L3, not a 1024²
row.

| shape | calls | hip µs | a16 µs | conv CSV µs | a16 vs hip | conv vs hip |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `3->96 @1024²` | 1 | 85.3 | — | 93.6 | — | 0.91x |
| `96->96 @1024²` | 10 | 417.7 | — | 262.6 | — | **1.59x** |
| `96->192 @512²` | 1 | 133.6 | — | 122.0 | — | **1.09x** |
| `192->192 @512²` | 9 | 190.5 | 256.1 | 202.0 | 0.74x | 0.94x |
| `192->384 @256²` | 2 | 84.9 | 99.5 | 104.6 | 0.85x | 0.81x |
| `384->384 @256²` | 8 | 150.8 | 174.8 | 189.3 | 0.86x | 0.80x |
| `384->384 @128²` | 18 | 49.1 | 56.9 | 65.5 | 0.86x | 0.75x |
| `384->32 @128²` | 1 | 23.9 | 21.4 | 31.1 | 1.11x | 0.77x |
| `16->384 @128²` | 1 | 10.0 | — | 15.9 | — | 0.63x |
| `96->3 @1024²` | 1 | 296.8 | — | 145.3 | — | **2.04x** |
| `96->96 @1025² s2` | 1 | 106.3 | — | 96.9 | — | **1.10x** |
| `192->192 @513² s2` | 1 | 52.1 | 62.3 | 66.8 | 0.84x | 0.78x |
| `384->384 @257² s2` | 1 | 49.1 | 56.9 | 68.3 | 0.86x | 0.72x |
| `384->192 @256²` | 1 | 90.9 | 113.0 | 109.0 | 0.80x | 0.83x |
| `384->192 @512²` | 1 | 342.0 | 446.0 | 417.5 | 0.77x | 0.82x |
| `192->96 @1024²` | 1 | 674.3 | 707.1 | 410.1 | 0.95x | **1.64x** |
| `384->384 @166²` | 18 | 68.3 | **81.5** | 91.2 | **0.84x** | **0.75x** |
| `96->96 @1328²` | 10 | 719.3 | — | 439.4 | — | **1.64x** |

384 / `K=3456`: conv ~0.75x of hip, a16 **0.84–0.86x**. Heuristic `@166²` was
0.67x on this hip arm. Weighted 1024² still beats hip via `96->96` and skinny
N.

#### How much of the 1.55x is the transpose

Kernel reads NDHWC only. NCDHW input pays a transpose no tile affects.
Original 12.00 / 310.37 ms include it; current CSV `us` does not.

`05f919868` NCDHW CSV = later tile + transpose. `ed7b5a5a8` NDHWC retune.
Same-layout tile-only A/B: **−0.95%** Qwen / **−0.78%** Wan unweighted, so
the CSV gap is the transpose.

| bucket | original flydsl | NCDHW CSV (kernel + transpose) | current NDHWC | kernel since the original | drop transpose | product |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen 1024², 10 shapes | 12.00 ms † | 9.71 ms | 7.76 ms | **1.24x** | **1.25x** | 1.55x |
| Qwen 1328², same 10 | — | 16.13 ms | 12.68 ms | — | **1.27x** | — |
| Wan 480×832, 8 shapes | 310.37 ms † | 235.51 ms | 200.91 ms | **1.32x** | **1.17x** | 1.55x |
| Wan 368×544, same 8 | — | 128.70 ms | 110.43 ms | — | **1.17x** | — |

Saved vs original flydsl: Qwen 4.24 ms, transpose **1.95 ms (46%)** (~half of
ln(1.55x)); Wan 8-shape 109 ms, transpose **35 ms (32%)** (~one third).

Transpose as a share of NCDHW (kernel + transpose): Qwen 1024² **20%**
(1.95 / 9.71 ms), 1328² **21%** (3.46 / 16.13 ms); Wan 480×832 **15%**
(34.6 / 235.51 ms), 368×544 **14%** (18.3 / 128.70 ms). Those eight Wan
layers have no stride-2 resample, so they sit below the 76-row retune:
**13% median / 20% summed / 50% peak** (peak = stride-2). Full CSV passes
513.1 → 409.4 ms (−20.2%).

1.55x is not all transpose: Qwen ~half kernel/tile since the three-way, half
transpose; Wan ~two-thirds kernel, one-third transpose.

### What the tile tuner added

`bench_conv_tuned_ab.py`, conv only (no NCHW→NHWC transpose), rotated inputs,
best of three, arms interleaved per shape:

**Weighted by calls per decode: 16842.5 us -> 15960.3 us, 1.055x.**

| shape | calls | heuristic | tuned | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `384->384 @166²` | 18 | 102.58 us | 86.55 us | **1.185x** |
| `96->3 @1024²` | 1 | 150.54 | 131.28 | 1.147x |
| `96->192 @512²` | 1 | 144.36 | 126.00 | 1.146x |
| `192->192 @512²` | 9 | 233.46 | 207.42 | 1.126x |
| `384->192 @256²` | 1 | 114.15 | 105.68 | 1.080x |
| `384->192 @512²` | 1 | 454.62 | 421.68 | 1.078x |
| `16->384 @128²` | 1 | 11.35 | 10.67 | 1.063x |
| `96->96 @1024²` | 10 | 307.40 | 296.68 | 1.036x |
| `96->96 @1328²` | 10 | 522.56 | 505.48 | 1.034x |
| `192->96 @1024²` | 1 | 505.92 | 489.17 | 1.034x |

Ten of eighteen shapes hit the table; the other eight land **0.984x–1.003x**
(miss = no-op; noise ~±1.6%). Nine of those ten took a non-power-of-two N
tile.

Largest gain: `384->384 @166²` (18 calls/decode). Heuristic conv 0.67x of the
stored hipBLASLt arm; a16 **0.84x** (81.5 vs 68.3 µs); NDHWC CSV **0.75x**
(91.2 µs).

### Scope and limits

- **bf16, forward only.** Grad tensors route to torch. These VAEs run
  `no_grad`.
- Tuned tables are per-model, keyed on the full conv shape including `bias`
  (compile-time). Anything else uses the heuristic.
- Benches time only; correctness is the op_test and the tuner's `errRatio`
  gate.
- `three_way.json` predates the tile table (conv arm = heuristic). Conv arm
  reproduces within 0.6% weighted; 5.5% slower than current HEAD.
